title: Grill-me needed: is lyaml a permitted exception to the no-Lua-runtime-dependencies rule, or should skills parse frontmatter without it?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about AGENTS.md section 3's dependency stance.

Question:
AGENTS.md section 3 states "Lua runtime dependencies are forbidden; use LuaJIT and stable Neovim APIs" and "mini.test is the sole test dependency". lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua requires lyaml, a Lua runtime dependency with a native LibYAML component, and the test suite cannot fully pass without it. Which side gives -- does the contract acquire a documented exception, or does skills stop depending on lyaml?

Context/evidence:
- discovery.lua:79 does pcall(require, "lyaml") and degrades to a structured missing_dependency diagnostic when it is absent, so the product does not crash without it. That graceful degradation is why the contradiction stayed invisible.
- It became visible only when the plugin got CI for the first time (8dbff06): a clean runner produced 36 failures across skills_spec, ui/chat_spec, ui/command_spec and health_spec, all cascading from the absent module (louiselm-zpsj, run 32735068144).
- The maintainer has since chosen to install lyaml in CI only and leave the clean-clone gap documented, which resolves provisioning but leaves the contract text untouched and now demonstrably false on both bullets.
- No approval trail was found for lyaml under section 3's "Any additional development dependency requires a demonstrated gap and explicit approval".

Threads worth pulling:
- Is the rule's real intent "no dependencies in the hot path / for things Neovim can already do", with an optional, gracefully-degrading parser being outside its spirit? If so the fix is precise wording, not an exception list that invites the next one.
- What would replacing lyaml cost? SKILL.md frontmatter is a narrow subset of YAML (scalars, lists, maybe nested maps). A hand-rolled parser removes a native dependency and the LuaRocks/LibYAML toolchain from every contributor's machine, at the price of owning a parser and its edge cases -- and of silently accepting some valid YAML that real skills might use.
- Does "mini.test is the sole test dependency" mean sole *direct* test dependency, in which case lyaml is a runtime dependency the tests happen to exercise and the bullet is merely imprecise rather than wrong?
- If lyaml stays, does the graceful-degradation path deserve stronger guarantees -- e.g. is a user without lyaml getting a usable skills experience or a quietly broken one?
close_reason: Maintainer decided lyaml stays and no hand-rolled parser will be built: correct frontmatter parsing is expected to become load-bearing for configurable workflows (louiselm-qbr.3), so weakening it is the wrong trade. AGENTS.md section 3 updated to name the exception.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Resolved by the maintainer, 2026-08-24: lyaml stays, and a hand-rolled frontmatter parser is explicitly rejected.

Decisive reasoning is strategic rather than about today's cost. Correct frontmatter parsing is not incidental to a skills feature -- it is likely to become load-bearing for the configurable-workflow work (louiselm-qbr.3), because a persisted workflow may itself be expressed as a frontmatter-carrying Markdown document, quite possibly a SKILL.md reusing the discovery mechanism that already exists. Owning a partial YAML parser under that assumption means the workflow substrate inherits its edge cases, and 'some valid YAML a real skill or workflow uses is silently misparsed' is a much worse failure than 'contributors install a rock'.

Note this also runs the other way: louiselm-m8a ('Support standard nested metadata in skill discovery frontmatter') already pushed this code toward the standard rather than a convenient subset, which a hand-rolled parser would have made progressively harder.

Consequence for the contract: AGENTS.md section 3's 'Lua runtime dependencies are forbidden' and 'mini.test is the sole test dependency' are updated to name lyaml as a deliberate, reasoned exception rather than left silently false. The restrictive intent of the rule is preserved -- this is one named exception with a rationale, not an open door.

title: DeepSeek token usage is absent from Session options
description:
A completed DeepSeek Session reports token usage on the ACP wire, but LouiseLM displays no observed usage in `:LouiselmSessionOptions` and creates no persistent usage ledger.

## Observed

Manual QA Case 7 on 2026-08-24, build `60724f3`:

- Agent Session: `deepseek/session-25790698-4242-41d4-af23-cfe0e512d90c`
- Primary log: `/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5/acp-llm-adapter/sessions/session-25790698-4242-41d4-af23-cfe0e512d90c/log.jsonl`
- Expected ledger: `/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5/nvim/louiselm/usage.json`

The untouched ACP log contains this structural evidence without requiring payload values:

```json
{"direction":"agent_to_client","kind":"frame","payload":{"id":3,"result_keys":["stopReason","usage"],"usage_keys":["cachedReadTokens","cachedWriteTokens","inputTokens","outputTokens","thoughtTokens","totalTokens"]}}
```

The expected `usage.json` file is absent after the completed turn. The tester sees no observed usage values in `:LouiselmSessionOptions`.

## Symptoms

- The user cannot see real DeepSeek token measurements beside Session options.
- No usage sample is persisted even though `session/prompt` returned token usage.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:328-357` reads snake_case names such as `total_tokens` directly from the ACP result. The real Agent sends ACP wire keys in camelCase (`totalTokens`, `inputTokens`, and related fields), so validation returns an empty internal usage table. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1957-1972` consequently has no measured token values to render or persist.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/api_spec.lua:644` invents a snake_case ACP response fixture. That matches LouiseLM's internal representation rather than the real wire payload, so the test validates the wrong boundary shape. UI tests likewise inject already-normalized snake_case state.

## Fix direction

Normalize the known camelCase ACP wire fields to the existing snake_case `TurnUsage` representation at the session validation boundary. Keep downstream presentation and storage in the existing internal form. Capture the real result shape in a regression fixture; do not make downstream code accept two naming conventions.

## Acceptance

- A regression test using the real camelCase result shape fails before the fix and passes after it.
- The completed Session shows a `[usage]` line for reported values.
- `:LouiselmSessionOptions` shows an observed token sample for the active option.
- The usage ledger is written under the configured state root.
- Malformed known token fields fail explicitly; unknown optional fields are ignored.

## Not covered

The same log also contains a `usage_update` with context and cumulative cost. Whether first-turn cumulative cost should become a per-turn option cost sample is separate from this token-key normalization and remains unverified. Raw log payload values are intentionally left in place rather than copied into this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A real-shaped ACP session/prompt result whose usage object uses camelCase token keys is validated and normalized into LouiseLM internal snake_case TurnUsage; the completed Session renders its reported usage and persists an option usage sample, while malformed known fields are rejected and unknown optional fields remain ignored.
close_reason: Normalize camelCase ACP usage keys to snake_case TurnUsage at validation boundary; regression test + malformed-field rejection added. Gates: stylua --check, lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning, MiniTest.run() all pass (473 cases).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Fixed in validation.lua turn_usage: reads ACP wire camelCase keys (totalTokens, inputTokens, outputTokens, thoughtTokens, cachedReadTokens, cachedWriteTokens) and maps them to internal snake_case TurnUsage; unknown fields ignored, malformed known fields fail. Updated api_spec fixture to the real camelCase shape and added a malformed turn-usage rejection test.

title: stylua --check . fails on main after the account-limits feature
description:
`stylua --check .` fails on main, so a required quality gate is red for every contributor and every
push. The violation is a single over-indented line in a test added with the account-limits feature.

## Observed

Repository root /home/lotso/code/louiselm at acb65c7, 2026-08-25, during the manual QA round for
60724f3..acb65c7.

    $ stylua --check .
    Diff in ./tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:
    35193519 |   })
    35203520 |   MiniTest.expect.equality(
    35213521 |     nvim.wait(1000, function()
    3522     |-          return nvim.tbl_contains(buffer_lines(0), "49% left · 51% used")
        3522 |+      return nvim.tbl_contains(buffer_lines(0), "49% left · 51% used")
    35233523 |     end, 1),
    35243524 |     true
    35253525 |   )

Line 3522 is indented with 10 spaces where StyLua wants 6.

Introduced by f8309a3 `feat(limits): surface Agent capacity` — inside the QA range under test, not
pre-existing relative to it. Two prior sessions saw the failure and recorded it as "pre-existing ...
outside this change" in comments on louiselm-zufj (2026-08-25 04:47 and 05:05 UTC), so it was
observed twice and carried forward twice rather than fixed.

CI enforces StyLua as a dedicated job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:51-55, added by 8dbff06). The last
recorded CI run is 0f1f26f at 2026-08-24T14:38Z, which predates f8309a3; origin/main is currently
e2f4c7c with no run listed by `gh run list`. So the gate is violated but whether CI has actually
gone red on the pushed head is unconfirmed.

## Symptoms

- `stylua --check .` exits with a diff instead of clean, which AGENTS.md section 4 lists as a
  mandatory gate.
- Any contributor running the documented gate before handoff sees a failure unrelated to their work,
  and the documented response is to report it — which is what happened twice, without resolution.
- CI's stylua job should fail on any push containing f8309a3 or later.

## Root cause

Formatting drift at tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:3522. Not a logic defect. The commit was authored and
landed without a clean repository-wide `stylua --check .`, and the two sessions that noticed it
scoped it out as someone else's problem rather than filing it.

## Why it was not caught

Nothing asserts the gate at commit time. There is no pre-commit hook, and CI apparently has not run
on the affected head, so the only enforcement point is a human running the command and choosing to
act on the result. Both humans-in-the-loop here were agents that reported it in a comment on an
unrelated bug, where no command reads it.

## Fix direction

Run `stylua .` and commit the single-line reformat. Nothing else in the tree is affected — the diff
is one line.

The durable half is the second-order problem: a failing shared gate reported inside a comment on an
unrelated issue is a report nobody acts on. AGENTS.md already says "emit, don't narrate" for work
noticed outside your scope; this is a concrete instance where the rule was not followed and the
consequence was two sessions of carry-forward. Consider whether the gate belongs in a pre-commit
hook so drift cannot land at all.

## Acceptance

- `stylua --check .` exits clean from the repository root.
- The CI stylua job passes on the resulting head.

## Not covered

- Whether CI has actually failed on origin/main is unconfirmed; `gh run list` shows no run for
  e2f4c7c or any commit after 0f1f26f. Someone should check why the workflow did not trigger, which
  may be a separate defect.
- lua-language-server and the mini.test suite were not re-run as part of this finding.
close_reason: done

comments.text: Fixed: ran `stylua .`, single-line reindent in tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:3522 (10 spaces -> 6). Verified clean: stylua --check . clean, lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning clean (no problems found), full mini.test suite 499/499 pass, 0 fails/notes. Committing now.

title: Concurrent ACP permission requests deadlock the session
description:
Two parallel tool calls in one agent turn produce two overlapping session/request_permission requests. louiselm opens one vim.ui.select picker per request with no serialization, so the second picker steals the first, the first is answered with outcome=cancelled without user input, and the second is never answered at all. The agent then blocks forever waiting on the permission response, and the session is unrecoverably stuck at status=prompting.

## Observed (session claude/25e0dc43-f1d6-4110-be74-e23b1d9920b7, 2026-08-16 19:45 UTC)

Agent JSON-RPC log ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260816-214042-74168-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:

- id=0  session/request_permission  find / -iname "*bc036951*"   -> answered (Always Allow), tool completed
- id=1  session/request_permission  wc -l ...gardening/....jsonl -> answered outcome=cancelled  (user did NOT choose this)
- id=2  session/request_permission  grep -n -i grill ...         -> NEVER answered

id=1 and id=2 were emitted back to back (19:45:12.63). Transcript
~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/25e0dc43-....jsonl records
"Tool permission request failed: Error: Tool use aborted" for toolu_01NgmPSjG8GXeMfmjuKrvfZZ (wc) 18ms after the grep tool_use, and has no tool_result at all for toolu_01K4jqsnByKAkCN5pJMRhRgU (grep).

Agent pid 74168 was still alive and blocked on id=2 more than 13 minutes later. The grep tool_call stayed "pending" forever; session/prompt never returned.

Proof the user never confirmed either choice: ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/permissions.json holds an always-rule for the find command only (mtime 19:45:04). Had the user actually confirmed "Always Allow" on the wc or grep picker, permission/store would have persisted a rule for it. It did not - the picker was dismissed programmatically, which is exactly what the user reported seeing ("a select picker that was pressed automatically and not by me").

## Symptoms

- Chat header shows "Model responding" forever; status=prompting.
- Typed input reports "Queued for next turn" and never runs, because Session:prompt requires status=="ready".
- One tool is reported to the model as aborted even though the user never denied it, so the model sees a bogus refusal.

## Root cause

1. lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:56 - every agent request is dispatched independently (nvim.schedule out of the fast event). No queue, no per-session serialization of session/request_permission.
2. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:732 prompt_permission -> lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua:11 calls vim.ui.select directly for each request. With an async provider (Snacks picker, which this setup uses) a second vim.ui.select while one is open tears down the first; its callback fires with nil -> cancel_permission responds outcome=cancelled to the wrong/first request, and the surviving picker never delivers a selection for the second request.
   Nothing tracks outstanding permission requests, so a request whose picker dies is never answered and never times out.
3. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:288 - permission_respond sets status back to "prompting" as soon as ANY single response is sent, regardless of other outstanding permission requests. That is why the UI showed "Model responding" instead of "Waiting for permission" while still blocking on id=2.

## Why tests miss it

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua stubs vim.ui.select with a synchronous callback (e.g. lines 172-188, 330-343), which serializes requests implicitly. Real async pickers do not.

## Fix direction

- Serialize permission prompts per session: queue incoming session/request_permission and open the next picker only after the previous one has been answered.
- Track every outstanding request id; guarantee exactly one response per request (fail-closed with outcome=cancelled on UI teardown/dispose so the agent is never left hanging).
- Keep status=="waiting_permission" while any permission request is still outstanding.
- Never let picker teardown cancel a request the user did not act on - prefer re-prompting or a queued prompt over a silent cancel.

## Acceptance

- Regression test with an async vim.ui.select stub that holds callbacks: two overlapping permission requests must produce two pickers shown one after the other and two responses, neither of them a spontaneous cancel.
- Test that disposing/closing while a permission is pending sends exactly one cancelled response per outstanding request.
- Test that status stays waiting_permission until all outstanding permission requests are answered.

## Recovery note

While stuck there is no documented way out except cancelling the turn; investigate whether Session:cancel actually unblocks an agent that is parked in session/request_permission.
close_reason: Fixed in c639f95. Sessions queue session/request_permission and publish one at a time (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua pump_permissions), status stays waiting_permission until the last outstanding request is answered, and a second response for the same request returns 'permission request was already answered'. Session:cancel now answers every outstanding request with outcome=cancelled, which is the recovery path the bug lacked. Remembered rules moved from arrival to publish time so an always choice covers requests already queued. Chat UI answers cancelled instead of dropping a choice made after view teardown. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua 'publishes overlapping permission requests one at a time', 'cancels every outstanding permission request when the turn is cancelled', 'applies a fresh always choice to permission requests already queued'; tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'cancels a queued permission choice after disposal'. Full suite 194 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. Deviation from the filed acceptance criteria: dispose clears the queue instead of writing cancelled responses, because dispose closes the ACP client and kills the agent process.

title: Permission picker Enter moves selection instead of confirming
description:
## Context

Observed in LouiseLM session codex/01a004ba-1d79-7a52-8d92-cec4cfdf1dc7 while committing. The permission picker displayed option 1 (Allow once) selected by default. Pressing Enter moved the option down in the picker instead of confirming it.

## Expected

Enter confirms the currently selected permission option and sends the ACP permission response.

## Actual

The selection/cursor moves down in the picker window; the permission is not immediately confirmed.

## Triage

LouiseLM delegates permission prompts to vim.ui.select. The current user Snacks config sets picker.sources.select.focus = "list" and enables wrap = true/linebreak = true. The recent permissions commit 757134a4 changed remembered-choice handling and option data, but did not change picker key handling. Likely interaction is in the Snacks select provider or its wrapping/focus configuration; reproduce with a minimal vim.ui.select containing the Codex options, then test with select wrapping disabled.

Relevant code: lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua prompt_permission() calls nvim.ui.select(options, ...).
Relevant docs: README.md explains Snacks select wrapping and recommends wrap = false for the select source when rows are not usable.
close_reason: Closed after reproducing with a very long permission option: Snacks vim.ui.select behaved correctly once picker source wrapping was disabled (wrap = false). The screenshot indicated keypresses had reached the underlying readonly chat buffer (E21), not a LouiseLM choice-handling failure. No LouiseLM bug reproduced.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Screenshot reproduction: Snacks picker shows 4/4 results but only two rows are visible in a very short list window; option 1 is highlighted. The underlying louiselm:// buffer reports E21 after attempting :verbose, which is expected because that buffer is nomodifiable; the command was not run in a command-line context. This points toward picker focus/list-window behavior or visual scrolling, not malformed permission choices.

title: Make reporting a session bug easy with a stable session identifier
description:
## Goal

Make it easy to report a louiselm bug against a specific session by telling the maintainer one stable identifier, instead of manually extracting context from the UI or conversation.

## Investigation

The current implementation has two different identifiers:

- The public session state exposes a local runtime id (`state.id`), which is not the ACP persistence id needed to correlate a resumed conversation.
- The agent-side ACP id is stored privately on the session (`acp_session_id`).
- The resume picker formats the title first and only falls back to the ACP id; the id is therefore not guaranteed to be the first visible item.

A bare ACP id may also be ambiguous when multiple configured agents can use the same id, so the most useful report token is the configured agent name plus the ACP session id (or an equivalent stable single-line representation).

## Proposed fix

Expose a deliberate, read-only report identity for the current session and make it easy to copy/quote:

1. Add a public session inspection field or method for the agent-side ACP session id/report identity, with LuaCATS documentation distinguishing it from the local runtime id.
2. Add a small user-facing command/action such as `:LouiselmSessionId` that reports the current session identifier and copies it to the Neovim clipboard when available; it should work for newly created and resumed sessions and fail clearly when no session is attached.
3. Put the report identifier first in the relevant session picker row, keeping title/workspace metadata available after it. Avoid exposing internal implementation fields directly or logging prompts/transcripts.
4. Document a short bug-report workflow: include the identifier, reproduction steps, and expected/actual behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can obtain one stable identifier for the currently displayed session with one command/action.
- The identifier remains useful after `:LouiselmResume` and identifies the ACP conversation, not merely the transient local session object.
- Agent identity is included when needed to avoid cross-agent ambiguity.
- The picker displays the report identifier as its first item/field.
- No prompt, tool payload, token, or other sensitive session content is copied or logged.
- Headless tests cover current-session, resumed-session, no-session, and picker-format behavior.
- README/help documentation explains how to include the identifier when reporting a bug.

## Follow-up

A separate grill-me session can stress-test whether a command, automatic bug-report template, or a richer session diagnostic bundle is the right UX before implementation expands beyond the minimal identifier workflow.
close_reason: Implemented stable agent-scoped ACP report identifiers. Public session snapshots expose acp_session_id; :LouiselmSessionId copies/reports <agent>/<ACP-id>; resume and attached-session picker rows lead with the report identity; README documents the bug-report workflow. TDD covered new, resumed, no-session, clipboard, and picker behavior. Full 131-case MiniTest suite passes; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server reports zero diagnostics; git diff --check passes; dependency graph has no cycles.

title: Document and diagnose Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Goal

Make Agent Skills configuration understandable and diagnosable for users of both known and unfamiliar ACP adapters.

## Scope

- In scope: update README skills/dogfooding sections, schema-generated help and annotations, migration guidance, and checkhealth.
- In scope: explain the three policies, native default, per-agent override, static sessions, natural-language versus picker activation, explicit-only skills, and the no-double-send contract.
- In scope: explain that Agent Skills specifies skill files, ACP is transport, and native command advertisement or Codex-like fallback behavior are host/adapter mechanisms rather than ACP skill specification features.
- In scope: document the fixed injected catalog behavior and 8,000-byte conservative Codex-inspired budget, including truncation/omission ordering and absolute-path privacy.
- In scope: provide platform-neutral `lyaml`/LibYAML installation guidance with common examples, Lua 5.1 ABI guidance for Neovim, no automatic install, and profile-specific missing-dependency effects.
- In scope: document root precedence, relative-path workspace trust, symlink aliases/escapes, skill-folder trust, `allowed-tools` permission limits, and the absence of automatic project roots or trust database.
- In scope: explain that injected implicit activation requires agent-side file access, picker-attached instruction-only skills may work without it, scripts/references/assets still need agent tools, and ACP does not standardize or let health verify this capability.
- In scope: show effective policy and detailed parser/discovery diagnostics in checkhealth, including shadowed/invalid skills, metadata conflicts, symlink escapes, line warnings, and catalog truncation/omission.
- In scope: document live-only fold contents and nofile/swap-disabled memory implications, plus manual installed Codex and Claude smoke procedures.
- Out of scope: authenticated adapter automation, a general ACP command UI, filesystem serving, and tool-call fold UX.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new user can choose `native`, `inject`, or `off` for an unfamiliar adapter from documentation alone.
2. Codex and Claude examples use native mode without duplicate injection; custom DeepSeek/GLM adapter examples show explicit inject overrides.
3. Old `full_content` users receive a direct migration explanation.
4. Checkhealth identifies actionable dependency, path, metadata, shadowing, and budget issues without claiming it can verify agent-side filesystem access.
5. Documentation explicitly labels the Codex-inspired budget/fallback as non-standard and leaves a future-spec reconsideration note.
6. Generated help/annotations and README configuration examples agree.
7. Manual smoke instructions verify native invocation with installed Codex and Claude adapters and injected behavior with a mock/custom adapter.

## Testing

Run documentation/schema consistency checks and health tests. Perform documented manual adapter smoke checks when credentials and installed adapters are available; do not make them CI requirements.
close_reason: Documented all Agent Skills profiles and trust/dependency behavior; added checkhealth catalog-budget diagnostics with tests.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Completed Agent Skills profile documentation and diagnostics. README now explains Agent Skills vs ACP/host behavior, policy choice for unfamiliar adapters, native Codex/Claude and injected DeepSeek/GLM examples, static/no-double-send semantics, explicit-only behavior, lyaml/LibYAML installation and Lua 5.1 ABI, profile-specific dependency effects, root/symlink/workspace trust, absolute-path privacy, agent-side filesystem/tool limits, non-standard 8000-byte fallback, live folds, checkhealth, and manual native/inject smoke procedures. Schema descriptions feed matching policy text to vimdoc and LuaCATS. Checkhealth now reports inject catalog bytes and exact shortened/omitted names. TDD: focused health test failed before implementation and passed after. Verification: 311 MiniTest cases pass; git diff --check and targeted StyLua pass. Whole-tree StyLua and LuaLS remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua (louiselm-d7l; LuaLS 9 warnings there, none elsewhere). Installed adapter shims found for Codex, Claude, and acp-llm-adapter; existing manual evidence includes native Codex session codex/01a01f0d-a7c6-75d3-b749-a21b9d4f8d31 and three real injected Codex runs in louiselm-yik. Claude/custom procedures are documented; credentials were not probed and authenticated automation remains out of scope.

title: Permission picker treats Allow Once as Deny
description:
## Summary

After the fail-closed permission ordering fix, a user who selects the displayed second option, Allow Once, can still send the first option, Deny. Generic vim.ui.select providers may render numbered rows without interpreting a typed number as row selection.

## Reproduction

Session: claude/d0cb6393-4548-4533-937f-614160f5a2b5

1. Ask Claude to perform an operation requiring permission.
2. Deny the first request.
3. Ask Claude to retry and select displayed option 2, Allow Once.
4. Observe Claude receives User refused permission again.

The ACP trace advertised Deny as option 1 and Allow Once as option 2 on both requests.

## Expected

A deliberate Allow Once choice sends its exact ACP optionId. Rejecting, allowing, and cancelling must all be unambiguous regardless of the installed vim.ui provider.

## Actual

Typing the displayed option number can confirm the provider current row instead, so option 2 is interpreted as option 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The permission choice flow does not depend on provider-specific numbered-row key behavior.
2. Choosing Deny sends the deny optionId, and choosing Allow Once sends the allow optionId.
3. Invalid or dismissed choices cancel rather than approve.
4. Agent option labels and identifiers remain distinct and unmodified.
5. Scheduled UI handling and late-choice-after-disposal safety remain covered by headless tests.
close_reason: Replaced provider-dependent permission selection with explicit numbered input, preserving exact ACP option IDs. Added regression coverage for Claude's Deny/Allow Once options, invalid and dismissed input, distinct labels, scheduling, and disposal. Verification: 43 focused UI tests and 184 full MiniTest cases pass; installed Snacks input smoke returns typed 2; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Investigate diff edit approval UX
description:
## Context

After asking LouiseLM to create a file, the plugin opened a `louiselm-diff` buffer. The latest screenshot (`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0457_1920x1200_1786244259.png`) shows the target path, `--- original`, `+++ proposed`, and an otherwise empty buffer. No visible accept/reject/close actions or instructions are presented, and Neovim is in insert mode.

## Investigation

Determine the intended lifecycle for an agent-proposed file edit and whether this diff view is currently incomplete, incorrectly rendered, or intentionally only a review surface. Trace the permission/edit/diff flow and document how a user should:

- understand what changed;
- accept/apply the proposed edit;
- reject it;
- cancel or return to the conversation;
- handle an empty/new-file diff;
- recover if the diff buffer is closed or the proposed edit becomes stale.

Assess the UX from a first-time user perspective, including discoverability of keymaps/commands, mode choice, statusline/help text, and whether approval belongs in the diff view, a permission prompt, or both.

## Exit criteria

- Reproduce the flow with a deterministic test or documented local scenario.
- Identify the root cause of the empty/unactionable presentation, if it is a bug.
- State the intended user-facing contract and recommended minimal UX changes.
- Add implementation follow-up beads tasks if the investigation finds separate fixes.
- Add or update headless UI behavior coverage for the confirmed contract where practical.
close_reason: Added discoverable diff approval instructions and normal-mode focus; verified full test and quality gates.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Investigation complete. The diff controller already had buffer-local normal-mode mappings: a accepts, d/q reject. The screenshot was unfriendly because the review buffer provided no instructions and inherited insert mode from the chat prompt, making those mappings undiscoverable/unusable. The diff is a permission review; accept sends the ACP allow response and the agent performs the write. Added an explicit instruction line and return to normal mode on focus. Existing behavior tests plus the new render assertion pass; no separate apply bug was reproduced.

title: Restored chat crashes while rendering replayed history
description:
## Problem

Loading an existing ACP/Codex session works, but the chat UI crashes when replayed assistant history arrives. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:690` performs arithmetic on `view.transcript_tail`, which is nil for a newly attached restored session.

## Reproduction

1. Create a session with Codex ACP and exit Neovim.
2. Load the ACP session with `sessions:load_session(...)`.
3. Attach it to `Chat`.
4. Observe `vim.schedule callback ... chat/init.lua:690: attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Restored assistant history renders without an error.
- New-session streaming behavior remains unchanged.
- Add a focused regression test covering a replayed chunk on an attached restored session.
close_reason: Fixed restored assistant chunk rendering fallback and added regression coverage. Focused chat tests: 30 passed; full mini.test suite: 115 passed; stylua --check and lua-language-server diagnostics passed.

title: QA round: protected quit guard
description:
# Manual QA review — protect multiple chat sessions from last-window quit

Working file for the current round. Untracked on purpose; it is scratch, live
only for this round.

**Build under test:** `5146007` (`fix(chat): preserve window on protected
quit`). Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: the commit adds a `QuitPre` guard so quitting Neovim from the only
window displaying a LouiseLM chat does not silently abandon multiple attached
sessions. It warns the user and asks them to switch or close a session first.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Block quit from the only chat window with two live sessions | **passed** — `:q` leaves the chat open |
| 2 | Allow quit after reducing the chat to one live session | **passed** — idle session closed without prompt; remaining chat stayed visible and `:q` exited |
| 3 | Do not block quit when another window exists | **passed** — chat window closed without protection warning |
| 4 | Do not block quit from an ordinary buffer | **passed** — ordinary buffer quit without protection warning |

## Setup

From the repository root:

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD
nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

The first command must print `5146007` (or a later commit containing this
fix). The interactive checks require a
working configured ACP agent; `manual_init.lua` uses the project's default
DeepSeek adapter unless the environment is configured otherwise. If the agent
cannot start, report the case as blocked rather than treating it as a product
failure.

Inside Neovim, run `:LouiselmChat`, wait for the first chat buffer/session to
open, then run `:LouiselmNewSession` and wait for the second session to open.
Use `:LouiselmSwitchSession` to confirm both sessions are attached before each
relevant case. Do not use `:qa!`: the guard is intended to protect ordinary
quit commands, while force-quit deliberately bypasses safety checks.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Case 1 is not reached unless `:LouiselmNewSession` has produced a second
  attached session. With only one session, `:q` closing Neovim is expected.
- After `5146007`, a protected quit briefly creates a duplicate chat window;
  the pending `:q` should close that duplicate and leave the original chat
  window as the only window.
- For Case 3, run the first `:q` while the statusline/buffer visibly shows the
  chat session. After it closes, confirm the remaining window is the ordinary
  buffer before running the final `:q`.

## Cases

### 1. Block quit from the only chat window with two live sessions

Exercises `41fec85` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmNewSession`, then run `:LouiselmSwitchSession`. The picker
   must show two session rows; cancel the picker after confirming this.
2. Ensure the current chat buffer has two live attached sessions.
3. Ensure Neovim has exactly one window (`:only` if needed).
4. Run `:q` (or press the normal window quit mapping).

Expect: Neovim remains open in the same chat buffer. A warning appears saying
that multiple sessions are open and instructing you to use
`:LouiselmSwitchSession` or `:LouiselmCloseSession`. The current session,
buffer, and chat contents remain usable.

Failure signature: Neovim exits; the chat window closes; no actionable warning
appears; or the warning appears but the quit still completes.

Evidence check:

```sh
git show --format= --check 41fec85
```

This confirms the committed patch has no whitespace errors, but cannot prove
that the interactive `QuitPre` callback stopped the quit; the visible result
and the still-running Neovim process prove that part.

### 2. Allow quit after reducing the chat to one live session

Exercises the disposed-session count in `Chat:should_block_quit`.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup so two sessions are attached in one chat window.
2. Run `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, select one session, then run
   `:LouiselmCloseSession` and confirm any prompt.
3. Confirm the remaining session is visible, then run `:q`.

Expect: the chat window closes and Neovim exits normally. No multiple-session
quit warning appears.

Failure signature: the warning still blocks quit after one session was closed;
the wrong session remains selected; or closing the session leaves a stale chat
buffer/window that prevents normal quit.

### 3. Do not block quit when another window exists

Exercises the `nvim_list_wins() ~= 1` boundary.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup with two live sessions attached.
2. Split the editor (`:split`) so there are two windows.
3. In one split run `:enew`, then use `Ctrl-w w` until the other split visibly
   shows the chat session (for example `session-2`). Run `:q` in that chat
   window.
4. Confirm the remaining window is the ordinary `[No Name]` buffer, then run
   `:q` again.

Expect: the first `:q` closes only the current chat window without a
multiple-session warning. The second `:q` exits normally.

Failure signature: the warning blocks the first window close despite another
window existing, or the chat/session state is unexpectedly disposed while the
first window closes.

### 4. Do not block quit from an ordinary buffer

Exercises the current-buffer attachment check.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup with two live sessions attached.
2. Open an ordinary buffer in the only window, for example with `:enew`.
3. Run `:q`.

Expect: Neovim exits normally without the multiple-session warning. This
confirms the protection applies only when the last window is displaying a chat
buffer attached to those sessions.

Failure signature: quit is blocked from the ordinary buffer, or a warning is
shown even though no chat buffer is current.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close any running agent processes and remove this scratch file after the round
is recorded in beads. Do not commit `QA_REVIEW.md`.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, exact command/keystrokes, what remained visible after the
command, and any warning/error text. If the agent could not start, include that
startup error separately.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Ordinary `:q` exits with two live chat sessions** (`louiselm-yk67`,
fixed in `5146007`).

With two sessions visible in `:LouiselmSwitchSession` and one chat window,
ordinary `:q` originally closed Neovim instead of leaving it open with the
actionable warning. The fix uses a temporary duplicate window because
Neovim's `QuitPre` event has no cancellation API. A regression test now
exercises the registered callback, and all four manual cases pass against
`5146007`.
close_reason: QA complete: all four manual cases passed against 5146007; finding louiselm-yk67 was fixed and closed.

title: Grill-me needed: what evidence should a LouiseLM bug report snapshot collect, preserve, and safely share
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing — it wants full attention.**

Raised as a side idea during the 2026-08-21 grill of `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. The user explicitly asked to preserve the idea without interrupting or replacing the foreground grill.

## The question

When LouiseLM is being used to debug LouiseLM, what explicit evidence/forensics manifest should guide an agent toward the recurring useful sources, and should a `:LouiseLmReportBug` command create a bounded local snapshot of those sources for diagnosis?

## Evidence from the session that raised it

The user has referenced one faulty LouiseLM session from another session while debugging the plugin. Given that reference, the model was already intelligent enough to navigate the available records and locate the relevant logs. The recurring retrieval pattern suggests product knowledge that should be made explicit and durable: enumerate the evidence sources an agent usually needs, retain provenance and relationships between sessions, and make collection reproducible instead of depending on a model rediscovering the filesystem layout each time.

This idea arose immediately after accepting coordinator-managed recovery of a known-dead worker, including a snapshot of that worker worktree and inspection of commits and uncommitted changes. Bug-report evidence may overlap with recovery evidence, but this issue must not pre-decide that they are the same artifact.

## Threads worth pulling

- Inventory the evidence that has actually proved useful in real failures before defining a bundle: referenced session records/transcripts and lifecycle state, ACP/process diagnostics, relevant LouiseLM logs, configuration facts, version/capability information, worktree/commit state, and a concise reproduction narrative. Treat this as a candidate list to validate, not an authorization to collect everything.
- Decide how session references are represented so a report can preserve the relationship between the diagnosing session and the faulty session without silently expanding collection to unrelated sessions.
- Separate an evidence manifest (knowledge of where and how to inspect sources) from a snapshot command (copying bytes). A manifest may be useful to an agent even when no bundle is created.
- Separate local snapshot from export/share. Local collection must not imply consent to upload, paste, publish, or attach anything. Any export path needs an explicit review/redaction step and a clear inventory of what will leave the machine.
- Make privacy and security first-class. Logs, prompts, transcripts, tool payloads, process environments, configuration, filesystem paths, credentials/tokens, and referenced sessions can contain sensitive data. Collection must be bounded, avoid credentials and full environments by default, preserve neither secrets nor unrelated session content merely for convenience, and fail closed when safe sanitization is uncertain.
- Establish retention, permissions, size/time bounds, destination ownership, and cleanup behavior for local snapshots. Avoid an unbounded recursive archive or a long-lived secret cache.
- Decide whether `:LouiseLmReportBug` is the right user interface, what it reports before collecting, and whether it should produce a human-readable inventory alongside machine-readable evidence. Do not assume the command name or archive format is settled.
- Preserve forensic integrity without claiming more than the implementation can prove: record timestamps/source paths and collection failures, do not mutate source evidence, and distinguish absent evidence from evidence deliberately omitted for privacy.
- Coordinate rather than duplicate `louiselm-ufx.2` (on-demand raw ACP payload inspection), `louiselm-06yh` (session/commit/beads linkage), and the worker recovery design in `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. Those are adjacent inputs, not owners of this support-snapshot boundary.

## Out of scope for this grill

Implementing the command, choosing the final evidence list from speculation, collecting current session data, exporting or sharing a bundle, or changing the live parallel-worker grill. React to the recorded requirement when this issue is deliberately opened.
close_reason: Grill completed with maintainer-confirmed shared understanding; implementation tracked by louiselm-ce6.24.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 1: call the concept evidence/forensics, not a manifest or bundle. The initial feature identifies relevant evidence in place and makes the retrieval knowledge explicit and durable; it does not copy artifacts into a snapshot. Snapshot creation remains a separate later decision if inspect-in-place evidence proves insufficient.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 2: each evidence/forensics record is anchored to exactly one subject Session, identified by Agent plus ACP Session ID. A different diagnosing Session may be recorded as provenance, preserving “Session B diagnosed Session A,” but must not be inspected or included automatically. Multi-Session incidents and whole-workspace collection are rejected as the default privacy boundary.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Security evidence: arbitrary ACP-log sanitization cannot justify a safe-to-share guarantee. The current acp-llm-adapter default recursively redacts only keys arguments/content/input/messages/prompt/text; plain stderr, malformed wire text, command-line args, and secrets under unexpected keys can remain. This denylist is useful exposure reduction, not a trust boundary. Candidate boundary pending maintainer confirmation: forensics may point to a raw local ACP log and allow deliberate local inspection, but must not automatically open, copy, summarize, embed, or export it, and v1 must make no sanitized-log claim. A later share/export feature should build a separate allowlisted typed report with user review; raw logs remain excluded unless knowingly attached.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 3: metadata and pointers are the normal evidence/forensics surface. Raw ACP logs are sensitive forensic artifacts: forensics may identify their local path and relevant safety metadata, but access is an explicit escalation and must warn that Agent inspection can disclose contents to its Provider. V1 does not automatically read, copy, summarize, embed, or export raw logs and makes no safe/sanitized claim. Adapter-side redaction remains useful exposure reduction only. Any future share/export feature emits a separate allowlisted typed report with user review; a raw log is included only by an explicit, informed attachment choice.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill correction: decision 3 is reopened because “explicit escalation before Agent inspection” conflicts with observed practice. Raw ACP payloads have repeatedly been useful, agent-friendly primary evidence during diagnosis. Revised candidate: choosing Session A as the subject of a diagnostic task authorizes the diagnosing Agent to inspect Session A’s raw ACP log as ordinary evidence, with bounded reads for relevance/size rather than privacy theater; no repeated per-read consent. The privacy boundary remains exactly-one selected subject Session, and the egress boundary remains copying/exporting/sharing outside the diagnosing Session. Metadata and pointers describe and locate evidence but do not replace access to primary evidence. Pending maintainer confirmation.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 3, revised and confirmed (supersedes comment 219): metadata and pointers make evidence discoverable but do not replace primary evidence. Selecting exactly one subject Session for diagnosis authorizes the diagnosing Agent to inspect that Session’s raw ACP log as ordinary forensic work, using bounded/targeted reads for relevance and size without repeated consent prompts. The privacy boundary prevents automatic inspection of unrelated Sessions. The consent boundary is export or sharing outside the diagnosing Session. Redaction is defense-in-depth only and carries no safe-to-share guarantee.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 4: evidence/forensics collection is read-only with respect to source evidence—the crime-scene rule. It must not move, rename, rewrite, truncate, delete, normalize, or clean up logs, transcripts, worktrees, or other sources. An explicitly created durable record stores bounded typed observations at collection time: subject/provenance identity, versions, cwd, Git commit/branch and dirty filenames, evidence paths, availability, size/timestamps where applicable, failures, and deliberate omissions. It contains no file contents or diffs. Naturally live or externally retained sources are labeled as mutable and observed-at, not falsely described as frozen or preserved.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Storage/view design candidate pending confirmation: correct the earlier assumption that collection automatically opens a human-readable view. Persist one canonical, versioned, typed JSON record per explicit collection under a private stdpath(state)/louiselm/forensics directory; do not persist rendered views or duplicate the evidence. The canonical structured record is the Agent-facing representation and includes explicit source kinds, paths, availability/mutability/sensitivity, observed facts, and retrieval guidance. A human-facing Neovim view is an optional projection of that same record, emphasizing subject/provenance, missing or sensitive evidence, and deliberate actions. Collection should return/announce the record identity/path; viewing is a separate concern. Existing lua/louiselm/workflow/evidence.lua stores routing-quality history and should remain semantically distinct rather than being reused.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 5: storage is one private, versioned, typed JSON record per explicit collection under stdpath(state)/louiselm/forensics. That canonical record is the Agent-facing representation, with stable evidence kinds, pointers, observed facts, availability, mutability, sensitivity, and retrieval guidance. Human presentation is an optional Neovim projection generated from the same record, emphasizing identity, chronology, missing/sensitive evidence, and deliberate actions. Collection returns the record identity/path and does not inherently open UI. Do not persist a second Markdown/rendered copy or reuse workflow.evidence routing-quality storage.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 6: collection is a headless/core operation taking Agent + ACP Session ID and returning a canonical record path or structured error; it does not depend on an open chat. A chat caller queues that path as an ACP resource_link for the diagnosing Session’s next prompt. An Ex-command caller outside chat reports the created path through normal Neovim command feedback, and a headless caller can print it to stdout. No prompt or analysis starts automatically. Diagnosing-Session provenance is absent when no diagnosing Session exists and may be established later when the record is attached. This preserves forensics when the chat UI itself is broken.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 7: each canonical forensics JSON record is immutable after successful creation. Re-collection creates a new timestamped observation rather than rewriting an earlier record. Records have no automatic TTL because explicit collection keeps their volume bounded and expiry would erase durable incident context; deletion is an explicit user action. Referenced source artifacts retain their own independent lifecycles and retention policies—the pointer record neither copies them nor extends their retention.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 8: collection is partial-success by design. Each expected evidence source records a typed state such as present, absent, inaccessible, unsupported, or deliberately omitted, including a bounded failure reason where useful. Missing evidence does not erase the rest of the record. The operation fails without a record only when the subject cannot be validly identified or the canonical record cannot be durably written. Discovery follows explicit Agent/Session metadata and known pointers; it must not scan broadly through the filesystem to guess missing evidence locations.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 9: the immutable forensics record contains collected observations and source pointers, not later interpretations. Reproduction narrative, hypotheses, diagnosis, remediation, and fix verification belong in a separate human/Agent-authored report or Beads work item that references the forensics record ID. This preserves the distinction between original observed evidence and conclusions drawn from it.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 10: durable configuration evidence uses a fixed typed allowlist rather than sanitizing or copying arbitrary configuration. Record Agent identity and reported name/version; known normalized capability flags; selected ACP option IDs with their current string/boolean values; cwd; Neovim/LouiseLM versions; and the agreed Git facts. Do not store raw capability payloads, option descriptions/catalogues, environments, prompts, tool payloads, full Agent definitions, or raw command arguments. Opaque primary evidence remains available for in-place inspection when diagnosis requires it.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 11: confirmed v1 surface. Provide a headless forensics.collect(Agent, ACP Session ID) operation; :LouiselmForensics defaults to the current Session or accepts Agent + ACP Session ID; collection reports the canonical JSON path and, when invoked with an attached diagnosing chat, queues it as resource_link context for the next prompt; :LouiselmForensicsView <record> renders the optional human projection. No bug-report workflow, snapshot/archive, export/share, record browser, or deletion UI in v1. Private immutable files may be explicitly removed through ordinary filesystem operations.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Shared understanding confirmed on 2026-08-24. Implementation is captured in feature louiselm-ce6.24 under the pure-ACP-client epic; canonical vocabulary record is louiselm-cvv3 (Forensics). No product-design questions remain.

title: CI: doc/api.md is stale, missing the thought_chunk EventType variant
description:
CI's required "lua-language-server" job fails at the "Verify generated API appendix" step because `doc/api.md` is out of date with the source it's generated from.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "lua-language-server", step "Verify generated API appendix":

```
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Reproduced locally on the same commit:

```
$ ./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
```

Running it without `--check` regenerates `doc/api.md` with this diff:

```diff
 louiselm.session.EventType:
     | "chunk"
     | "user_chunk"
+    | "thought_chunk"
     | "tool_call_started"
     | "tool_call_finished"
     | "permission_requested"
@@ -390,9 +391,9 @@ louiselm.session.EventType:

 ### louiselm.session.GenericEvent

-- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk" this is the raw ACP
+- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk"/"thought_chunk" this is
 - `session_id: string` -- Local session identifier.
-- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"|"turn_done"...(+1)`
+- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"thought_chunk"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"...(+2)`
```

## Symptoms

- CI reports the required "lua-language-server" job red on every push, independent of what the push actually changed.
- Exact error text: "doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix".

## Root cause

`louiselm.session.EventType` gained a `"thought_chunk"` variant as part of the reasoning-fold feature (commit `c56805f`), but `doc/api.md` was never regenerated to match — `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` (which the "lua-language-server" CI job runs with `--check`) diffs the committed file against a freshly generated one and fails when they differ. The regeneration command was not run before that commit (or a later one) was pushed.

## Why it was not caught

AGENTS.md section 4 lists `stylua --check .`, `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`, and the `mini.test` run as the direct local quality gates; it does not call out `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` as one of them, even though CI enforces it. Nothing in the documented pre-commit checklist would have caught this locally.

## Fix direction

Run `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` and commit the resulting `doc/api.md`. Separately, consider adding `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` (and `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check`, see the related nightly-Vimdoc bug) to the documented local gates in AGENTS.md section 4, since both are already enforced in CI but currently only discoverable by reading `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Acceptance

- `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` exits 0 on the fix commit.
- CI's "lua-language-server" job goes green on the next push.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes; filed separately.
- Whether other generated-doc drift exists elsewhere in the repo was not audited.
close_reason: fixed in 1395bfd. Regenerated doc/api.md via ./scripts/generate-api-appendix; --check now exits 0. Verified generate-vimdoc --check, stylua --check, and full mini.test suite unaffected (all green).

title: Codex reasoning chunks duplicate headers and fragment chat prose
description:
Codex reasoning updates corrupt the live chat after a tool call: the view renders one `[thinking]` header for each consecutive reasoning chunk instead of one collapsed reasoning paragraph, and the following assistant response is fragmented into one word/fragment per line with blank lines. This makes a normal Codex answer difficult to read. Reproduced in the currently attached Codex Session.

## Observed

Seen on 2026-08-26 in the live Neovim instance, Session `codex/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810` (local view `session-3`, buffer 306), after its completed tool call and while the Session was `ready` at turn 1.

Live buffer evidence, lines 185-188, contains four consecutive `[thinking]` headers. Lines 190 onward contain the answer with every visible word/fragment separated by blank lines. The live state reports `thought_folds=1`, four visible headers, and six transcript blocks (`user`, `reasoning`, `assistant`, `tool_call`, `reasoning`, `assistant`), so the displayed structure is inconsistent with the recorded reasoning paragraphs.

Raw ACP evidence is retained at `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810/log.jsonl` (156455 bytes, modified `2026-08-26 06:25:53.823794861 +0200`). Lines 60-63 are four adjacent `agent_to_client` `session/update` frames with `sessionUpdate="agent_thought_chunk"` and text lengths 2, 45, 2, and 50; they are followed by `agent_message_chunk` frames at lines 64-70. The log has six thought frames total (lines 15, 16, 60-63). No reasoning text is copied here because it may be sensitive; the local log is the primary artifact.

## Symptoms

- A Codex user sees four `[thinking]` labels rather than one collapsed reasoning section for contiguous thought updates.
- The assistant answer that follows is visually split into isolated words/fragments with blank lines, rather than streaming as readable prose.
- The Session's transcript structure says there is one second reasoning block, while the visible buffer presents four headers.

## Root cause

Unknown. `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:219-222` correctly maps ACP `agent_thought_chunk` to the typed `thought_chunk` event. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2232-2272` is responsible for maintaining `view.thought_run`, rendering its one header, and appending subsequent chunks. The observed four headers mean that run state is being closed or lost between adjacent Codex frames, or that the live loaded renderer differs from this checked-out path. The adjacent frame ordering above distinguishes this from an Agent emitting four separate reasoning paragraphs. The simultaneous fragmentation of later message chunks may share the same rendering/state-boundary failure, but that is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:674-719` directly emits two adjacent `thought_chunk` events through a synchronous fake session and asserts one header. It does not replay the captured Codex post-tool multi-frame sequence (four adjacent thought chunks followed by streamed message chunks) through the production ACP callback/scheduling boundary, nor assert that the rendered post-reasoning prose remains contiguous.

## Fix direction

Reproduce with a sanitized fixture preserving the observed event order from log lines 60-70. Trace the live event-to-render boundary to establish why `view.thought_run` does not persist. Fix the narrow shared rendering boundary so contiguous `thought_chunk` events produce exactly one header/fold and following `chunk` events append readable prose. Do not normalize or persist raw reasoning just to work around the presentation bug.

## Acceptance

- A regression test based on the observed Codex frame order fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Four contiguous `agent_thought_chunk` updates after a completed tool call render exactly one `[thinking]` header and one collapsed fold.
- The following streamed `agent_message_chunk` updates render as contiguous prose with no inserted blank line between ordinary word/fragments.
- The live Codex Session reproducer displays one collapsed reasoning section and a readable assistant answer.

## Not covered

- The exact mechanism that clears `view.thought_run` is not yet proven.
- Other Agents and Codex versions were not tested.
- Raw reasoning content remains only in the local ACP log and is intentionally not duplicated into this bead.

title: Winbar clicks never work via real mouse click: v:lua.require(...) is not a valid click-function name
description:
## Symptom

No winbar click has ever worked through an actual mouse click in Neovim -
not the session-switch tabs, not the Limits click segment. Clicking produces
no error, no session switch, nothing. Discovered while manually QA'ing the
`437fbf0` cross-window click-routing fix (case 6) - that fix is itself
correct, but sits downstream of a click mechanism that was never wired up
correctly in the first place, so there was never a live click to route.

## Evidence

Isolated with two throwaway winbar click regions, independent of any
louiselm code, to bisect which part of the click wiring is at fault:

1. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.qa_click_test_handler@[CLICK ME]%X"` (a plain
   global function reference) - click worked, handler fired.
2. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.require('qa_click_mod').handler@[CLICK ME 2]%X"`
   (the exact same shape as this codebase's actual click target string) -
   click did nothing at all.

Confirms Vim's `%{N}@{Function}@` winbar/statusline click syntax requires
`{Function}` to be a plain dotted name it can resolve at click-dispatch
time, not an arbitrary Lua call expression like `require('mod')` embedded in
that field.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:306`:

```lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click"
```

This constant has existed since `7b31438` "feat(ui): show Session attention
in winbar" - the winbar-click feature has apparently never worked via a real
mouse click since it was introduced, only in unit tests that call
`M.winbar_click(...)` directly (bypassing Vim's actual click dispatch, so
the broken click-target string was never exercised).

## Fix

Expose a stable global Lua function (not a call expression) as the click
target, forwarding to the reassignable `M.winbar_click`:

```lua
-- command.lua
_G.__louiselm_winbar_click = function(...)
  return M.winbar_click(...)
end
```

```lua
-- init.lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.__louiselm_winbar_click"
```

Found and being fixed during manual QA round, case 6.

title: ACP session options and resource telemetry UX
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM can select an adapter only when the first chat is created, and it currently discards ACP session configuration options and usage/context updates. Users cannot change an agent-advertised model or reasoning setting after startup, cannot see which settings are active, and cannot tell whether a long autonomous session is approaching its context limit or waiting on a permission request. Starting multiple sessions also lacks explicit navigation and cleanup controls.

## Solution

Add a generic ACP session-controls and observability UX. After `session/new` becomes ready, open a token-free setup overview of all supported agent-advertised select and boolean options; allow idle-only changes through a public chat method and `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, refreshing the complete option list after each update. Add explicit `:LouiselmCancel`, `:LouiselmNewSession`, `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, and `:LouiselmCloseSession` commands. Keep existing sessions running when a new one starts, expose their state through compact headers and switcher rows, and dispose sessions explicitly when closed. Render passive context-pressure states, reported cumulative cost, active settings, lifecycle state, permission waiting, compaction/tool activity, and optional experimental per-turn usage fields without estimating tokens or prices.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to choose model and other ACP session options before my first prompt, so that each new session starts with deliberate settings.
2. As a user, I want to change supported options while a session is idle, so that future turns use the new configuration without restarting the session.
3. As a user, I want busy sessions to refuse option changes and offer explicit cancellation, so that autonomous turns are not reconfigured mid-flight.
4. As a user, I want to see active settings, lifecycle state, context pressure, cost, and reported usage, so that I can monitor long-running work.
5. As a user, I want to create, switch between, and close concurrent sessions, so that multiple adapters can work without leaking processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A ready new session with supported ACP config options opens an overview picker before the first prompt; Esc accepts agent defaults and an agent with no supported options skips the picker.
2. The overview renders every supported select/boolean option in agent order, supports selecting values, applies `session/set_config_option`, replaces the local list with the complete response, and handles agent-pushed `config_option_update` notifications.
3. Option changes are rejected while prompting, cancelling, or waiting for permission; `:LouiselmCancel` requests cancellation and late callbacks cannot revive disposed UI or sessions.
4. The client advertises boolean config-option support and ignores unknown future option types while rejecting malformed consumed fields.
5. `:LouiselmNewSession` chooses an adapter, creates a separate session, and opens its setup picker without cancelling existing sessions; `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects attached sessions using compact agent/state/options/context/cost rows.
6. `:LouiselmCloseSession` confirms only for active or permission-blocked sessions, disposes the selected session/process, removes its chat buffer, and leaves other sessions running.
7. Session headers show exact lifecycle/activity state, all active options, context used/size/percentage with passive 75/90/95% warning states, stale context after model changes until refreshed, and reported cumulative cost when available.
8. Completed turns append a compact usage footer only for reported fields; optional experimental usage fields are validated defensively, never estimated or supplemented with adapter-specific fallbacks.
9. Compaction remains agent-owned: render generic ACP tool/compaction activity and context-meter changes, but add no LouiseLM manual compaction API in this phase.
10. Headless session snapshots/events expose typed configuration, lifecycle, permission, context, cost, and usage state for a future monitor; no swarm dashboard or orchestration is included.

## Implementation Notes

- Extend the session lifecycle and ACP validation at the shared boundary; preserve complete option-list replacement and asynchronous main-loop scheduling.
- Enrich `session:inspect()` and typed events rather than deriving telemetry from rendered buffers.
- Keep `LLM_MODEL` in the caller-owned schema/config example; do not add a universal built-in schema that rejects provider-specific environment variables.
- Preserve agent-provided defaults, session history, cumulative cost, and existing slash-command passthrough. Mark context telemetry stale after model changes until the agent reports a new effective window.

## Testing Notes

- Add focused mini.test coverage for option parsing, dependent option refresh, boolean capability advertisement, malformed/unknown options, idle-only transitions, cancellation, permission waiting, and disposal/late results.
- Add headless UI smoke tests for setup/overview flow, command behavior, headers, passive thresholds, usage footer omission, compaction/tool rendering, multiple-session navigation, and close confirmation.
- Exercise ACP notifications and process callbacks through scheduled production boundaries; use the mock ACP agent and no real credentials or agent binaries.

## Out of Scope

- Manual compaction or a hard-coded `:LouiselmCompact` command.
- A generic advertised-command picker.
- A swarm dashboard, orchestration, capacity policy, worktree isolation, or subagent aggregation.
- Adapter-specific usage parsers, pricing tables, tokenizers, or cache-cost estimates.
- A universal built-in configuration schema.
close_reason: Implemented ACP select/boolean session options, typed lifecycle/context/cost/usage state, setup and multi-session commands, safe scheduled UI updates, documentation, and passing StyLua/LuaLS/95-test gates

title: QA round: account limits, terminal results, Handoff and discovery through acb65c7
description:
# Manual QA review — louiselm.nvim, 2026-08-25

**Build under test:** `60724f3..acb65c7` (43 commits). Confirm with
`git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse --short HEAD` = `acb65c7`.

You drive; I read the evidence and edit this file every round. Both this file
and `qa_init.lua` are scratch under `/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/`; neither
gets committed.

Origin: the last round was `louiselm-0aft` (2026-08-24, build `60724f3`). Since
then the plugin gained **Agent account limits** end to end (parser, registry
capability/notification handling, winbar segment, `:LouiselmLimits` detail view,
threshold alerts, reset timers), **terminal tool-result rendering** for Copilot's
`task_complete`, **text-result signposting**, **Handoff transcript retention with
source provenance**, **resumed-turn usage replay**, **standalone proposal review
controls**, **session-picker recency ordering and injected-title recovery**, and
**embedded-resource skill catalogs**. Forensic log folding was added and then
reverted (`963ef07`/`0827979` → `a531705`/`771484a`) — out of scope, do not test.

CI enforcement, AGENTS.md rules and beads bookkeeping changed too. Not manually
testable; excluded deliberately, not forgotten.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Codex account limits reach the winbar and the detail view | **passed** — real 89%/7d bucket rendered as expected; `<Tab>` was a recipe misread, completion works |
| 2 | An unsolicited limits notification refreshes presentation | **partial** — notifications arrived and were accepted, nothing crashed, but the value never moved so re-render is unproven |
| 3 | Agents without the capability stay silent; empty snapshot says so | **passed** — copilot issued zero limits frames, claude returned `{"buckets": []}` |
| 4 | Copilot's `task_complete` conclusion is readable in the transcript | **FAILED** — F1: conclusion still not rendered; `task_complete` arrives 2.1s after `end_turn`, so `turn_done` flushes nothing |
| 5 | Handoff is retained in the target transcript with source provenance | **partial** — retention and edit fidelity confirmed; F3: provenance names `session-1`, not the durable id |
| 6 | A resumed Session replays per-turn usage in the right order | **passed** — ledger byte-exact against the wire, first `[usage]` sits after turn 1 |
| 7 | Session picker sorts by recency and recovers injected subjects | **ordering passed; F4 found** — `:LouiselmResume!` fails `session/list` on every strict Agent |
| 8 | A standalone proposal diff can be applied, discarded, and restores focus | **passed** — focus restored on both paths; stale guard preserved the file byte-for-byte |

## Round constants

Run everything from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.

Cases 1–6 and 8 share one pinned state root so their evidence stays together and
case 6 can resume what case 1–2 created:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state \
  nvim -u /tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/qa_init.lua
```

Case 7 deliberately runs **without** the override — it needs your real session
history. Its steps say so again.

After each launch:

- `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME` must print `/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state` (cases
  1–6, 8). If it prints something else the process did not inherit it; say so
  before running the case, because every evidence path below is wrong then.
- `:checkhealth louiselm` — `acp-proxy`, `node`, `copilot` must resolve. A
  missing executable is a setup blocker, not a product failure.

Evidence roots, once you have an ACP session id from `:LouiselmSessionId`
(format `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`):

```sh
LOG=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<acp-session-id>/log.jsonl
USAGE=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/nvim/louiselm/usage.json
```

`ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1` is set, so these logs contain your real prompts. Report
paths and session ids; do not paste log bodies into chat.

## Ground rules

- Fresh Session per case unless a case says to reuse one. A remembered
  permission or a prior routing decision changes the path under test.
- The Session-options picker appears on ready; note whether it is coherent, then
  dismiss it. Dismissing keeps Agent defaults on purpose.
- Tool payload inspectors are ordinary floating windows: close with `:q`, not
  plain `q`.
- Report what you saw verbatim, including text you think is irrelevant. Winbar
  spacing and punctuation are load-bearing in case 1.

---

## 1. Codex account limits reach the winbar and the detail view

Exercises `600e3d8`, `de04317`, `f8309a3`, `4e79797` — `session/limits.lua`,
`registry.lua:471-708`, `ui/limits.lua`, `ui/chat/init.lua:660-690`.

Codex is the only configured Agent that returns real quota buckets. A recent
real snapshot had one bucket `codex`, one window at 89% used over 10080 minutes.

Steps:

1. Launch with the pinned root above.
2. `:LouiselmChat`, select `codex`. Dismiss the options picker once ready.
3. Read the winbar of the chat window and copy it verbatim.
4. Run `:LouiselmLimits` with no argument.
5. Type `:LouiselmLimits ` and press `<Tab>`; note the completion list.
6. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and save the id.

Expect: a winbar segment shaped `limits codex 11%/7d ↻6d` — literally
`limits <bucket> <remaining>%/<window> ↻<time-to-reset>`, appended after the
status/context/cost segments. Colour is green above 20% remaining, amber at
20%–10%, red at or below 10% or when a limit is reached. `:LouiselmLimits` opens
a detail buffer for `codex` listing the bucket, each window's used percentage,
duration and `Resets:` as an absolute time plus a relative one, the plan type,
and the reset-credit count. `<Tab>` completes to the configured Agent names.

Prediction to confirm or refute (`4e79797`): there is a **space before `↻`**. If
you see `11%/7d↻6d` you are running a stale plugin copy, not `acb65c7` — stop
and tell me.

Failure signature: no limits segment; a segment stuck on `limits loading` or
`limits unavailable` that never resolves; `:LouiselmLimits` reporting *could not
inspect Agent account limits*; `Resets: reset time passed` for a reset that is
plainly in the future; an `E5560` fast-event error in `:messages`.

Evidence — I will run this once you give me the session id:

```sh
grep -h account_limits "$LOG" | head -5
```

This settles two things without your interpretation: that the read request went
out with `"params": {}` — a JSON **object**, which is exactly the `de04317` fix
— and what the Agent actually answered. What the winbar *renders* rests on your
report; the log only proves what arrived.

---

## 2. An unsolicited limits notification refreshes presentation

Exercises `registry.lua:handle_agent_notification`, `lifecycle.lua:181-190`,
`ui/chat/init.lua:793-893`.

Codex pushes `_io.github.euri10.louiselm/account_limits/updated` on its own after
consuming quota. Nothing in the test suite proves the UI reacts to a real one.

Steps (same Neovim, same codex Session as case 1):

1. Leave `:LouiselmLimits` open in a split if you can, so you can watch it.
2. Submit: `Read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md and list the four bullets
   in section 11 verbatim.` (absolute path on purpose — a bare filename makes
   the Agent search first and may not consume enough quota).
3. When the turn completes, read the winbar and the detail buffer again.

Expect: the used percentage and/or reset time move without you re-running any
command, and an open detail buffer updates in place rather than needing a
reopen. If a window crosses 20% or 10% remaining you also get a `louiselm:`
notification naming the Agent, bucket and window.

Prediction to confirm or refute: `handle_notification` now calls into the
registry for **every** ACP notification before filtering for `session/update`.
If the registry ever errors there, all session updates stop. Watch for the
transcript freezing mid-turn while the Agent is plainly still working.
