title: tests/ui/command_spec.lua has no post_case hook, so one failing test cascades into seven more
description:
Every case in tests/ui/command_spec.lua opens a chat buffer and cleans it up
by calling delete_chat_buffers() as its last statement. MiniTest aborts a case
at the first failed expectation, so a case that fails before that line leaves
its "louiselm://<id>" buffer open, and every later case that opens a chat
buffer dies with:

  Vim:E95: Buffer with this name already exists
  lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1616

Observed 2026-08-21 while writing the louiselm-euj regression test: one
genuine assertion failure produced 9 reported failures, 7 of them pure
cascade. The real failure was third in the list, and the cascade failures name
a different file and line than the test that actually broke, which is actively
misleading when reading a red run.

Workaround used in the two tests added for louiselm-euj: call
delete_chat_buffers() before the assertions rather than after. That works but
relies on every future author remembering it, and the existing cases in this
file all still have the fragile ordering.

Fix direction: give T["command"] a hooks table with a post_case that calls
delete_chat_buffers() (and ideally restores vim.ui.input / vim.notify /
vim.system, which have the same abort-leaks-state problem), then drop the
manual trailing calls. MiniTest runs post_case hooks even when a case fails,
which is the property the manual call lacks.

Worth checking whether tests/ui/chat_spec.lua and the other UI specs share the
shape before fixing, so this is done once rather than per file.

title: Chat buffer filetype=markdown lets image.nvim re-scan the whole transcript on every keystroke
description:
Typing in the louiselm chat buffer's prompt line is noticeably laggy, at rest
-- not during active LLM response streaming. Reported by the user mid-session
while typing with no chunks arriving.

## Observed

Session claude/6a76322f-4f96-430b-93f3-578808c4692c, 2026-08-20, connected
directly to the user's live `nvim --embed` instance over RPC
(`/run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0`) to inspect real state instead of guessing.

Ruled out with direct measurement, in order:
- `render-markdown.nvim` (installed in dotfiles) is not loaded at all:
  `luaeval('tostring(package.loaded["render-markdown"] ~= nil)')` -> `false`.
- Buffer size/decoration overhead is trivial: the chat buffer (bufnr 12,
  `louiselm://session-1`, filetype `markdown`) was 714 lines / 121121 bytes,
  with only 7 extmarks total (all in louiselm's own `louiselm.chat.header`
  namespace). Treesitter highlighter was active but on a buffer this small
  that's not a plausible lag source.
- System load: `uptime` showed load average 0.60/0.52/0.32 on a 16-core
  machine, `free -h` showed 20Gi available of 27Gi, 0B swap used. Not resource
  contention.
- No LSP clients attached to the chat buffer:
  `vim.lsp.get_clients({bufnr=12})` returned empty.

What IS confirmed present:
`nvim --server /run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0 --remote-expr
"luaeval('table.concat(vim.tbl_map(function(a) return a.event .. \"|\" ..
(a.group_name or \"-\") .. \"|\" .. (a.pattern or \"*\") .. \"|\" ..
tostring(a.buflocal) end,
vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event={\"InsertCharPre\",\"TextChangedI\",\"CursorMovedI\"}})),
\"\\n\")')"` listed, among 12 global autocmds on those three events:

  TextChangedI|image.nvim|*|false

A global (non-buffer-local, pattern `*`) TextChangedI autocmd owned by
image.nvim.

## Symptoms

- User sees: typing in the chat prompt feels unresponsive, specifically
  while it is their turn to type (no active stream).
- System reports: nothing -- no error, no warning. Silent per-keystroke cost.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366` sets the chat buffer's `filetype` to the
literal `"markdown"`:

    nvim.api.nvim_set_option_value("filetype", "markdown", { buf = buffer })

`~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/image.nvim/lua/image/integrations/markdown.lua`
registers image.nvim's markdown integration for `filetypes = { "markdown",
"vimwiki" }` (see `default_options.filetypes` in that file, wired up via
`document.create_document_integration`). That integration's
`query_buffer_images` function runs on every `TextChangedI` event: it calls
`vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf, "markdown")`, `parser:parse(true)`, and then
walks the full `markdown_inline` tree with two treesitter queries
(`(image (link_destination) @url) @image` and the shortcut-link variant),
looking for markdown image syntax to render inline in the terminal.

Because the chat buffer's filetype is the real `"markdown"`, image.nvim
cannot distinguish it from an actual markdown file the user is editing. It
therefore re-parses and re-queries the buffer's entire inline tree on every
character typed in insert mode, searching for images that don't exist and
never will in a live chat transcript -- pure, unconditional, per-keystroke
waste, scaling with growing transcript length as a session goes on.

`lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27` has the identical pattern
(`nvim.bo[buffer].filetype = "markdown"`) on a second buffer, but that buffer
is short-lived and not continuously growing/streamed like the chat buffer, so
it is noted here as the same root-cause class but not fixed by this bead.

## Why it was not caught

No test in the suite exercises interactive typing latency in the chat
buffer, or asserts anything about which global autocmds/integrations attach
to it. This class of defect -- a buffer silently opting into a third party's
filetype-keyed behavior it never intended to invite -- has no automated
signature; it only surfaces as felt input lag during real interactive use,
which is exactly how it was found here (user report, not a failing test).

## Fix direction

Give the chat buffer a distinct filetype (e.g. `"louiselm-chat"`) instead of
the real `"markdown"`, so filetype-keyed third-party integrations (image.nvim
today, anything else keyed on `ft=markdown` later) do not attach to it at
all, then explicitly re-attach markdown treesitter highlighting via
`vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")` (which takes the language
explicitly and is decoupled from `filetype`), so syntax highlighting is
preserved.

Rejected: asking image.nvim to opt out per-buffer instead. Would require
depending on that specific plugin's own opt-out mechanism (if any), and would
not protect against the next filetype=markdown-keyed plugin the user's config
gains later. Fixing the buffer's own identity is the narrower, more durable
fix and is entirely within this repo's control.

## Acceptance

- `nvim_get_autocmds({event={"TextChangedI","InsertCharPre","CursorMovedI"}})`
  filtered to ones matching the chat buffer's new filetype returns none from
  image.nvim (or any other third-party ft=markdown integration).
- The chat buffer still renders with markdown treesitter highlighting
  (verified via `vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[bufnr] ~= nil` after
  `Chat.new():open()`/equivalent).
- No existing test in `tests/` asserts the chat buffer's filetype is the
  literal string `"markdown"` (confirmed absent before this fix; grep
  `tests/` for `filetype.*chat\|chat.*markdown` stays empty after too).

## Not covered

- `lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27`'s identical pattern is not fixed
  here -- noted as the same root-cause class, lower priority given that
  buffer's short-lived usage pattern, left for a separate bead if it proves
  to matter in practice.
- Whether other globally-registered filetype=markdown integrations besides
  image.nvim (render-markdown.nvim, markdown linters, etc.) were also
  incidentally attaching -- render-markdown.nvim was directly confirmed not
  loaded in this session, but was not re-checked after the fix; not every
  possible third-party integration in the user's config was enumerated.
close_reason: Fixed: chat buffer filetype changed from the literal "markdown" to "louiselm-chat" (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366), with vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown") added explicitly to preserve highlighting independent of filetype. Root cause: image.nvim's markdown integration keys off filetype in {markdown, vimwiki} and re-parses/re-queries the whole buffer's markdown_inline tree on every TextChangedI event; the chat buffer no longer matches. Regression tests added: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'uses a distinct filetype, not the literal markdown third parties key off' (failed before the fix, confirmed) and 'keeps markdown treesitter highlighting despite the distinct filetype'. Full suite: 237/237 pass. luacheck: 59 warnings, all pre-existing, 0 introduced. stylua --check: clean. Not covered by this fix, as filed: lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27 has the same pattern on a different, short-lived buffer -- left open per the bead's 'Not covered' section.

title: CI: nvim-nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness check fails while stable passes on the same commit
description:
The advisory "mini.test (nvim nightly)" CI job's "Verify generated Vimdoc" step fails, but `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes cleanly when run locally against nvim stable on the same commit — suggesting the check's result differs between nvim stable and nvim nightly rather than the doc actually being stale.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "mini.test (nvim nightly)", step "Verify generated Vimdoc":

```
louiselm Vimdoc is stale; run ./scripts/generate-vimdoc
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

This step runs identically in the "mini.test (nvim stable)" job (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, both `stable` and `nightly` are the same matrix job differing only in `neovim: ${{ matrix.neovim }}`), and it passes there — only the nightly leg fails.

Reproduced (partially) locally: `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` exits 0 with nvim stable installed locally, on the same commit (fd1d606) where the nightly CI leg reports it stale. Nightly was not installed locally to cross-check directly.

## Symptoms

- The nightly matrix leg of "mini.test" reports failure on "Verify generated Vimdoc", though this job has `continue-on-error: true` for `matrix.neovim == 'nightly'` (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so it does not fail the overall required checks — it only shows as a red/crossed-out leg in the Actions UI.

## Root cause

Unknown — not yet isolated. Hypotheses:

1. `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (or the `:helptags`/doc-generation machinery it drives) produces byte-for-byte different output between nvim stable and nvim nightly (e.g. a changed `:h` formatting default, a Lua stdlib behavior change nightly introduced), so the committed `doc/*.txt` matches stable's output but not nightly's.
2. The nightly Neovim build used by `rhysd/action-setup-vim@v1` in that run had a transient/unrelated regression unconnected to the actual doc content.

What would discriminate: install nvim nightly locally (or in a disposable container) and run `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` directly against it, then compare its regenerated output to the committed doc file to see the actual diff.

## Why it was not caught

The documented local gates (AGENTS.md section 4) run against local/stable Neovim only; there is no local nightly Neovim in the loop, so a stable-vs-nightly divergence in generated-doc output is invisible until CI's nightly leg runs. Because that leg is advisory (`continue-on-error`), a failure there produces no blocking signal and is easy to miss entirely — this was only noticed because of an unrelated report about the required jobs failing on the same run.

## Fix direction

Not yet chosen — depends on which hypothesis above holds. If it's genuine stable/nightly output drift in the doc generator, the fix likely lives in `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (make its output version-independent, or gate the `--check` comparison on stable only). If it's a nightly build flake, no code fix is needed, just noting it as expected nightly noise.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified with a reproduced diff (or confirmed flake) rather than a hypothesis.
- `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes on nvim nightly in CI, or the check is explicitly scoped to stable only with a documented reason.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the stale-`doc/api.md` failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes (both on the *required* stable/lua-language-server jobs); filed separately. This bug is lower priority since the affected job is advisory and does not block merges.

title: Show attached Session attention in the chat winbar
description:
## Problem Statement

When several Sessions are attached, the user can see only the current Session status without opening the Session picker. Permission requests, completed background responses, and failures can therefore wait unnoticed.

## Solution

Show a right-aligned, clickable strip for attached background Sessions in every LouiseLM Session winbar. Keep all Sessions visible when space permits, make attention states visually prominent, and preserve the existing picker as keyboard and overflow navigation.

The strip is always enabled when at least two Sessions are attached and absent with one. Entries use the renamed Session title when present, otherwise the Agent name. ACP Session IDs are not shown.

A completed response becomes attention-worthy only when its turn_done event occurred while the Session was not focused. Focusing that Session acknowledges the response. Permission and error attention persist until resolved or disposed.

## User Stories

1. As a user working in one Session, I want to see all other attached Sessions so I know their state without opening a picker.
2. As a user, I want permission requests, unseen completed responses, and errors to stand out so I notice required action.
3. As a user, I want to click a Session entry to switch directly to it.
4. As a user in a narrow window, I want attention-needed Sessions protected from overflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given one attached Session, its winbar remains the existing single-Session presentation with no background strip.
2. Given two or more attached Sessions, every Session is represented by the current Session segment or a clickable background entry when width permits.
3. Clicking a background entry switches the window to that Session; keyboard users can continue to use :LouiselmSwitchSession.
4. A renamed Session uses its name; otherwise its Agent name is shown; ACP Session IDs are omitted.
5. Ready and seen Sessions use a green dot, active Sessions use a blue ellipsis, unseen completed responses use a yellow dot, permission requests use a yellow exclamation, and errors use a red cross.
6. A background turn_done marks that Session unseen; focusing it clears only that completed-turn attention.
7. Permission attention remains until answered and error attention remains until resolved or disposed.
8. Under width pressure, labelled attention entries remain visible, quiet entries collapse into a neutral clickable +N entry, and +N opens the Session picker.
9. Repeated setup, Session changes, window changes, and disposal do not leak handlers or mutate unrelated winbars.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse the existing Session event stream, status highlights, winbar renderer, Session picker, and rename state.
- Track unread completion state in the Chat UI owner, not the core Session lifecycle: attention is presentation-specific and depends on window focus.
- Use stable Neovim APIs and marshal editor operations through existing scheduling boundaries.
- Add no configuration option, dependency, compatibility shim, or speculative extension point.

## Testing Notes

- Extend behavioral headless chat tests.
- Cover background turn completion versus initial ready state, focus acknowledgement, persistent permission/error attention, direct click routing, overflow priority, disposal, and scheduled UI rendering.
- Preserve existing single-Session winbar behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Global tabline or statusline integration.
- ACP protocol changes.
- Desktop notifications, animation, sound, or user-configurable visual themes.
- Replacing the existing Session picker.
close_reason: Implemented and verified clickable multi-Session attention winbar

title: Resume picker hides last-updated time at line end
description:
In the session picker opened by `:LouiselmResume`, the last-updated timestamp is placed after the session title and cwd, so long titles consume the available width and hide the timestamp. Users cannot quickly tell which resumable Session is newest without moving to the far end of the picker line, which is especially painful in a narrow picker.

## Observed

Screenshot evidence captured 2026-08-24 at 09:31 local time after running `:LouiselmResume`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0931_1920x1200_1787556713.png`

The selected row visibly contains:

`is your next best task · cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm · updated=2026-08-24T06:54:07.000Z`

and the `updated=` portion is at the far right, beyond the useful visible width for long rows. The lower row shows the same layout with `updated=2026-08-23T19:09:52.000Z` after the title and cwd.

Source path inspected: `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`, where `discovered_session_summary()` appends the cwd and then the updated timestamp after the title.

## Symptoms

- The resume picker shows session identity/title first, then cwd, then `updated=`.
- Long titles push the recency information out of view.
- The user must navigate to the end of each picker line to compare when Sessions were last updated.

## Root cause

Confirmed in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`: `discovered_session_summary()` builds the display parts in the order agent/session id, title, cwd, updated timestamp. The timestamp is therefore the least likely field to remain visible when the picker width is scarce.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:1980` asserts a full summary string but does not exercise display behavior with a constrained picker width or a long title that obscures the trailing metadata.

## Fix direction

Change the summary ordering at `discovered_session_summary()` so the last-updated information appears before the long title/cwd fields, while preserving enough session identity to distinguish rows. Keep the result compact; do not solve this by requiring horizontal navigation to inspect recency.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after, asserting that `updated=` precedes the title and cwd in the discovered-session summary.
- In a picker with scarce width and a long session title, the last-updated value is visible near the beginning of the row without navigating to the line end.
- Session identity remains visible and existing resume selection behavior is unchanged.

## Not covered

The exact compact timestamp format and final ordering of title versus cwd are implementation choices. This report does not require changing picker width, truncation behavior, or the underlying persisted timestamp.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Reordered discovered_session_summary() in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua so updated= appears immediately after the session identity, before title and cwd, keeping recency visible in scarce picker width. Regression updated in tests/ui/chat_spec.lua and failed before the implementation change. Focused chat suite: 105/105. Full MiniTest suite: 469/469. Gates: stylua --check . and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning pass. Existing test-environment warnings about a missing temporary grill-me skill and clipboard/write output remain unrelated.

title: Enter does nothing with a visible draft in a ready resumed chat
description:
A resumed louiselm chat can display an intact non-empty draft under a ready session while buffer-local Enter produces no ACP prompt and no visible error. The affected user cannot continue that session through the primary chat path, although the agent process remains healthy and the draft is recoverable.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-21 in live Codex ACP session `01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101`, Neovim 0.12.2, louiselm buffer on `/run/user/1000/nvim.1020915.0`.

Read-only live probes returned: `name=louiselm://session-1`, `mode=i`, `modifiable=1`, `line=598`, `line_count=598`, `last_len=181`, `last_prefix=> can you ch`, and insert `<CR>` mapping description `Submit louiselm prompt` with a buffer-local callback. `undotree()` reported `seq_cur=268`, `seq_last=268`; the user reported using normal-mode `U` and `Ctrl-r` before the failure.

The Codex rollout `/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/20/rollout-2026-08-20T17-39-25-01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101.jsonl` ends with `task_complete` at `2026-08-20T16:55:34.216Z` and contains no later user turn. The adapter log `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-173923-1021245-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` contains no later `session/prompt`; the live `codex-acp` and Codex app-server processes remain running. `v:errmsg` is empty and `:messages` contains no louiselm submission error.

## Symptoms

- Header says `Your turn`; typing works, but pressing Enter appears to do nothing.
- Draft remains visible and no prompt reaches ACP/Codex.
- No error explains why submission was rejected or skipped.

## Root cause

Unknown. The failure is below Codex and after louiselm rendered the ready state, but it has not yet been discriminated between (a) the key callback not executing despite the installed mapping, and (b) `Chat:submit()` reading an empty or wrong range because `view.prompt_line` is plain Lua state while normal-mode undo/redo mutates only the buffer. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:722` reads from `view.prompt_line`; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1637` installs the Enter callback; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1910` silently returns for an empty prompt.

## Why it was not caught

Chat tests call `chat:submit()` directly and exercise buffer edits, but there is no behavioral test that drives the installed Enter mapping after real normal-mode undo/redo in an attached/resumed transcript. Empty-prompt rejection is also silent at the keymapping boundary.

## Fix direction

First capture the failure in a headless UI test that feeds the actual mapping after transcript changes and undo/redo. At the narrowest boundary, make the prompt location track buffer edits (for example, an extmark owned by the view) or explicitly prevent transcript undo from invalidating UI state. The Enter callback must surface any returned submission error instead of silently appearing dead. Do not patch Codex or restart the adapter as the evidence shows no request reaches it.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves Enter submits the visible draft after `U`/undo and redo on a ready attached or resumed chat.
- The prompt sent to the fake ACP session exactly matches the visible draft and prior transcript text is never included.
- If the draft cannot be resolved, Enter emits one actionable louiselm error rather than doing nothing.
- Existing queueing, multiline prompt, and resume tests remain green.

## Not covered

The exact key event has not been injected into the live user session because that would submit their draft. A clean synthetic 1:1 undo/redo probe did not reproduce the defect, so the live undo branch and callback-vs-boundary hypotheses remain unverified. No code fix is included in this diagnostic.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Root cause: the prompt boundary was a Lua row number, so undoing streamed transcript lines left submission reading past the visible draft; a left-gravity extmark now tracks the boundary and the real Enter mapping test passes after :undo. title: Codex edit permissions are answered with a -32602 protocol error
description:
codex-acp sends edit permission requests with no reviewable payload at all:

  {"toolCall":{"toolCallId":"call_SObIFxWtTS90EE6K7JbBTfgX","kind":"edit","status":"pending"},"options":[...]}

(from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260717-163626-2991539-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log)

No rawInput, no content, no path. lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua from_acp therefore returns {kind = "file_edit", path = nil}, gates.check rejects it with "permission file edit must have a non-empty path", and lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_request answers the agent with JSON-RPC error -32602 instead of asking the user anything. The user never sees a prompt and codex sees a protocol error.

Separate from the claude case: there is nothing to review here, so the fix is not a better diff. A file-edit request that carries no path or reviewable text should fall back to the generic permission picker (allow/reject options are present in the payload) rather than being answered with a protocol error.

Found while fixing the claude payload bug; not verified live with codex, only from the logged payload and reading the code.

title: Grill-me needed: should manual QA rounds use a native louiselm://qa-review workspace
description:
Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this question in passing.

Should manual QA rounds use a native `louiselm://qa-review` workspace instead of making a long `QA_REVIEW.md` file the tester's primary interface?

## Context and evidence

During the 2026-08-24 manual QA round, Case 5 required different setup from earlier cases. A shared Setup section forced the tester to navigate backward and reconstruct which commands applied. The screenshot at `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0708_1920x1200_1787548138.png` shows the practical cost: separate panes for the QA recipe, LouiseLM Session under test, setup terminal, and conversation/evidence, with the current case detached from the setup it needs.

The immediate process improvement is clear: every case should be self-contained and repeat its exact launch, reset, action, and evidence-capture steps. A small global constants section may hold the build and scratch-state path, but completing a case should never require scrolling elsewhere to reconstruct its apparatus.

## Threads to pull

- Is the native buffer a transient controller/view while Beads remains the durable round and finding record?
- Which case-local actions belong in the buffer: launch recipe, pass, fail, blocked, retest, next, cleanup?
- How should keyboard navigation and commands work for a human tester without turning the interface into a second test framework?
- How should Agent Session IDs and Forensics pointers be captured without copying, rewriting, or exposing raw evidence?
- When and how should findings be created and parented to the QA round?
- What survives editor restart, and who owns cleanup of scratch state and test Sessions?
- Does `QA_REVIEW.md` remain as a generated/exportable view, or disappear?
- How does the same structure remain legible to an Agent performing analysis and a human intervening at the keyboard?

title: Malformed ACP file-edit permission request terminates session
description:
## Reproduction

In session codex/019ff53a-629d-71a3-a1de-1a2506b42912, the agent sent an ACP session/request_permission file-edit request without a non-empty path. louiselm reported:

`Error: invalid ACP permission request: permission file edit must have a non-empty path`

The invalid request currently calls the session fatal-error path, closes the ACP client, and prevents the grilling session from continuing.

## Expected

Reject only the malformed permission request with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error. Keep the ACP session alive so the agent can continue or retry with a valid request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A file-edit permission request with a missing or empty path receives an error response with code -32602 and the validation message.
- The session remains ready/waiting for subsequent work and does not emit a fatal session error.
- Existing valid permission requests and malformed fatal startup/update handling remain unchanged.
- Add deterministic regression coverage.

title: Render a session transcript into an editable handoff prompt buffer
description:
## Goal
Render a live session's transcript into an editable buffer that becomes the first
prompt of another session, with nothing sent until the user submits.

## Scope
- In scope: turning `Transcript:snapshot()` entries into buffer text; opening it
  for editing; submitting the edited buffer as a prompt to a target session;
  abandoning it without sending.
- Out of scope: choosing the provider, creating the target session, and the
  user command -- all in the sibling task. This task is the payload half only.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a session with recorded entries, a buffer is produced containing the
   transcript with full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries.
2. Nothing is sent to any session while the buffer is open.
3. Submitting sends exactly the buffer's current contents, so edits are honoured.
4. Abandoning the buffer sends nothing and leaves both sessions untouched.
5. An empty buffer refuses to send with an actionable message rather than
   prompting with nothing.

## Testing
Headless: entries in, buffer text out; edit-then-submit sends the edited text;
abandon sends nothing; empty refuses. Assert on the payload actually handed to
the session, not on buffer appearance.

## Notes
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` (`snapshot`, `render`) and
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript_export.lua` already turn entries into markdown
untruncated; reuse rather than write a third renderer. Check whether
`Transcript.render` is directly usable before adding anything.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p. The review step is a
hard requirement, not a convenience: it is both the disclosure gate and the way a
wrong frame gets cut before it contaminates the second provider.
close_reason: Completed: added editable transcript handoff buffers with edit-and-submit, abandon, empty-input rejection, and cleanup; focused and full mini.test suites pass

title: Wire the provider handoff command and keep the source session attached
description:
## Goal
Wire the handoff command: pick a target provider, open a session on it, feed it
the reviewed transcript buffer, and leave the source session attached.

## Scope
- In scope: the user command and its error paths; the provider picker excluding
  the current agent; creating the target session through the existing
  `new_session` seeding path; handing the buffer from the sibling task to it;
  keeping the source session attached and switchable.
- Out of scope: rendering the buffer (sibling task), capability routing, and any
  automatic or policy-driven switching.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The command opens a picker of configured providers excluding the current one,
   and does nothing on dismissal.
2. The target session is created through the same path as `new_session`, so
   initial contexts, skill catalog, and instructions context are seeded, and the
   target provider's own `skills_policy` is applied rather than the source's.
3. The source session stays attached and reachable through the existing session
   switcher after the handoff.
4. Errors are distinct and actionable for: no chat session, an open permission
   decision, a non-idle source session, fewer than two configured providers, and
   target session creation failure.
5. A test proves a permission remembered for the source agent does not apply to
   the target agent.
6. No command, option, or user-facing string uses "model" to mean provider.
7. README documents the command in the interactive-controls list.

## Testing
Headless with the mock ACP agent configured twice under different names. Cover
each error branch, the dismissal path, source-session survival, and permission
isolation. Async paths must exercise the production callback context.

## Notes
Depends on the buffer task; wire against its interface rather than reimplementing
rendering.

Naming: the maintainer's earlier phrasing was `:LouiselmModelChange`, which was
the wrong word and cost a reverted implementation (louiselm-model-change-cl59,
db39f96). Repository convention is verb-first --- `LouiselmSwitchSession`,
`LouiselmRenameSession`, `LouiselmPickSkill` --- so something like
`:LouiselmSwitchProvider` or `:LouiselmHandOff` fits. Confirm the name with the
maintainer before implementing; do not infer it.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p.
close_reason: Wired :LouiselmHandOff end to end: picker excluding the current agent, target session created via the existing new_session seeding path, source stays attached/switchable, distinct errors for every listed case, permission isolation proven by test, README updated. See implementation-notes comment for file-level detail.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Command name confirmed with maintainer: :LouiselmHandOff. Rejected :LouiselmSwitchProvider -- the picker is over named agent config entries, not vendors; two entries can share a provider/binary and differ only in model (e.g. codex/Luna vs codex/Sol), so 'provider' would misdescribe what's being picked. 'Handoff' names the mechanic (hand the conversation to another configured entry) without asserting what changed underneath. PascalCase per repo convention (LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmPickSkill).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Implementation notes: wired :LouiselmHandOff (chat:hand_off()) in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua. Reuses chat:new_session(agent_name) for target creation (same seeding path, target's own skills_policy applied) after resolving the target via a Picker.select excluding the source agent. Errors: disposed, open permission decision (DECISION_OPEN_ERROR), no chat session attached, non-idle source (status ~= ready or a queued prompt), fewer than two configured agents, and target creation failure (notified async in the picker callback, source untouched). Permission isolation across agents proven in tests/permission_spec.lua (store-level, per the parent's implementation decision that this needs no new mechanism, only a test). README documents the command. No 'model' wording anywhere. Full mini.test suite (351 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server all pass.

title: Resumed Sessions omit completed-turn usage
description:
A Session shows a [usage] line after each live completed turn, but those lines disappear when the same Agent Session is closed and resumed. A new turn after resume produces a new usage line; the completed-turn telemetry from earlier turns is what is lost.

## Observed

Subject Session: deepseek/session-5b4fb715-7267-4f09-848b-54e84fca2dfc on 2026-08-24.

Primary evidence: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/3b75a6dd-f56b-407c-84ad-f9194c74e416.jsonl.

- Line 3 is session/load request id=2 for the subject Session.
- Line 161 is its response; result keys are _meta, configOptions, and modes, with no completed-turn usage.
- Replay includes conversation/tool chunks and usage_update notifications, but those usage_update values are context/cost telemetry, not the completed-turn input/output/thought/cache breakdown.
- Line 2086 is the subsequent live prompt response id=3 and contains totalTokens=624499, inputTokens=621517, outputTokens=2982, thoughtTokens=1706, cachedReadTokens=21888, cachedWriteTokens=599629. LouiseLM rendered exactly those values as [usage].

The adapter Session history has 294 entries and zero usage-bearing entries. LouiseLM state usage.json has 14 aggregate records, but its schema contains neither session_id nor turn identity.

## Symptoms

- Live completed turns show [usage] total_tokens=... with the provider breakdown.
- Closing and resuming the Session replays the conversation without those usage lines.
- Completing another turn after resume shows usage for only that new turn.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua assigns state.usage only from a live session/prompt result in handle_prompt_result. Loaded Session state starts without usage, and on_session_ready consumes configOptions but no turn usage. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua appends [usage] only while handling live turn_done. lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua intentionally ignores turn_done and usage events. lua/louiselm/workflow/usage.lua persists aggregates by Agent option value, not by Session or turn, so it cannot restore the annotation.

## Why it was not caught

The resume tests cover replayed user/assistant/tool content but expect no usage annotations. Usage tests cover only live session/prompt results and aggregate persistence; no test closes and reloads a Session after a measured turn.

## Fix direction

Persist completed-turn usage under the stable Agent plus ACP Session identity when it is received, and restore the corresponding visible annotation during replay. Do not infer the detailed breakdown from usage_update context telemetry or from Agent-wide aggregates.

## Acceptance

- Completed-turn usage observed by LouiseLM survives closing and resuming the same Agent Session.
- Restored usage remains associated with the correct turn and retains all reported fields.
- A new post-resume turn appends its own usage without duplicating restored usage or aggregate accounting.
- Sessions created outside LouiseLM or turns recorded before persistence exists degrade cleanly when no usage is available.

## Not covered

ACP session/load does not provide historical completed-turn usage for this Agent, so LouiseLM cannot reconstruct telemetry it never persisted.
close_reason: Loaded Sessions now expose their validated ACP identity at construction, allowing Chat:attach to read exact persisted turn usage before replay.

comments.author: codex/01a03349-c229-74e2-8d06-81fb2d016869
comments.text:
Workflow reflection after live confirmation on 0534977:

The first implementation persisted the right data but solved a narrower interpretation than the maintainer was testing. The requested outcome was observable: resume the same Session and find the prior per-turn [usage] lines in the view. Aggregate option samples and newly emitted post-resume usage were neighboring signals, not acceptance.

A full grill-me was not required for this focused defect, but a one-sentence acceptance lock was: “Resume the same Session; searching \\[usage finds the previously displayed per-turn lines beside the correct turns; the lines remain client-only; aggregate samples are separate.” Without that lock, automated evidence was allowed to substitute for the actual view.

Two test doubles then hid two production orderings. The first omitted intermediate historical state_changed events, so it missed scheduled handlers reading a later mutable Session snapshot. The second manually supplied acp_session_id before Chat:attach, so it missed the asynchronous load identity race. The regressions became trustworthy only after they reproduced those structural timings without copying sensitive Session payloads.

The efficient debugging path is now clear: inspect the exact live view first; trace one value end to end from prompt result to usage ledger to Session identity to replay turn to buffer line; encode the real ordering in a regression; and keep the bug open while the exact live reproduction remains available, until the maintainer confirms it. Diagnostic- or tracking-only commits must be called out as non-retest builds so commit movement is not mistaken for behavior movement.

Engineering invariants exposed by this bug: scheduled event handlers decide from the immutable event payload, not a later mutable Session snapshot; and an asynchronously loaded object exposes identity already known and validated at construction immediately.

title: Grill-me needed: How should Agent account limits cross the pure-ACP boundary?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused design decision before implementing account-limit transport.

Question:
How should structured Provider account-limit state reach LouiseLM while preserving the core pure-ACP boundary and enabling both Codex and, where possible, Claude?

Context and evidence:
- The accepted human UX contract is recorded on louiselm-u56l.
- The core epic louiselm-ce6 says LouiseLM is a pure ACP client and that non-ACP capabilities arrive through external bridges, never in-plugin Provider adapters.
- Codex App Server provides account/rateLimits/read and account/rateLimits/updated with the required structured data.
- Installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 receives and caches that structured data but exposes it only as rendered /status text, not as a structured ACP event.
- Parsing /status would bind behavior to prose and is rejected.
- Starting a Codex App Server sidecar inside LouiseLM would provide data quickly but introduces a Provider protocol into the pure ACP client and does not generalize to Claude.
- A provider-neutral structured ACP extension emitted by external Agent adapters would preserve the boundary and give Codex and Claude a shared normalized contract, but requires adapter work and a clear capability negotiation/fallback rule.

Threads worth pulling:
- Standard ACP extension mechanism versus a LouiseLM-namespaced method or session update.
- Capability advertisement and behavior for Agents that do not implement account limits.
- Whether the external adapter normalizes Provider data or forwards a lossless Provider payload.
- Ownership and deduplication when several Sessions share one Agent or account.
- Versioning, validation, sparse updates, and compatibility with other ACP clients.
- Which repository owns the codex-acp and Claude adapter changes and how LouiseLM tests them deterministically.

Decision boundary:
Choose the cross-process contract and ownership. Human UX is already decided. AX and automated switching policy remain separate follow-up work.
close_reason: Maintainer accepted a capability-advertised, provider-neutral ACP custom extension owned by external Agent adapters.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: 2026-08-24 protocol finding: ACP v1 officially supports extension methods. Custom request and notification names must start with underscore, unrecognized notifications are ignored, and extensions should advertise support in agentCapabilities._meta. Source: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/extensibility. LouiseLM already preserves the agentCapabilities table and its ACP transport can send arbitrary request methods and receive arbitrary notifications; session lifecycle currently ignores non-session/update notifications. codex-acp uses the ACP SDK custom-handler path already for other extensions, and its schema preserves _meta, so adding a limits extension is structurally supported. Recommended boundary: external Agent adapters advertise a versioned provider-neutral account-limits capability, answer an underscore-prefixed read request, and emit an underscore-prefixed updated notification. The adapter owns Provider-specific parsing and sparse-update merging, and sends a complete normalized snapshot. LouiseLM validates snapshots and owns Agent-level freshness, UI, notification deduplication and source failover across live Sessions. This preserves the pure-ACP core, avoids /status parsing and sidecars, and lets a Claude adapter implement the same contract. Stock codex-acp 1.6.2 must be changed before the live Codex slice can work.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Decision accepted by maintainer: use the official ACP custom-extension mechanism. External Agent adapters advertise a versioned Provider-neutral account-limits capability in agentCapabilities._meta, answer an underscore-prefixed read request and emit an underscore-prefixed update notification. Adapters own Provider parsing and sparse-patch merging and emit complete normalized snapshots. LouiseLM remains a pure ACP client and owns validation, Agent-level source selection/state, freshness, UX and notification deduplication. Incubate under a collision-resistant LouiseLM namespace; pursue ACP standardization separately only if broader adoption warrants it. No sidecar and no rendered-text parsing. Lesson routing: this decision is already enforced by parent epic louiselm-ce6 pure-ACP boundary and the child feature; no duplicate AGENTS.md rule is warranted now.

title: QA round: session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring
description:
# Manual QA review — session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring

**Round closed 2026-08-20.** All ten cases (0–9) run. Six findings, two fixed
and verified during the round, four filed and deliberately left open. This is
the round's sole durable record; the working file it was written in has been
deleted, per `louiselm-ri1`.

**Build under test:** `ec19281..HEAD` (15 commits). The ones with testable
behaviour:

| Commit    | What changed                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `6167df0` | writefile errors in `Chat:to_markdown` (re-verify, `louiselm-dim`)   |

Doc/bookkeeping only, nothing to test: `ec86d89`, `a515c01`, `e9d801a`,
`3140b93`, `b1f2781`, `a8af349`, `10ba83c`, `e0c6269`, `0d53644`, `9856288`,
`cd47617`.

**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the last round (`louiselm-vj0`) closed on build `4e4a58b`/`674939b` and
produced two fixes that were never re-driven by hand. Since then the chat
buffer's filetype changed under every filetype-keyed plugin the user has
installed, and the export format grew raw HTML — both changes whose real

one plugin's cost for another's absence, and the trade needs to be deliberate.

**Partial result.** The blast radius is far smaller than assumed. Exactly one
autocmd is registered against `FileType markdown`:

```
MystMarkdownFiletype: Override markdown filetype if MyST content detected
```

from `myst-markdown-tree-sitter.nvim` (`~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/myst-markdown.lua`).

wrong — it was inferred from a stale `render-markdown.log` dated Aug 3.)

**Result: PASS.** The two readings are byte-identical:

```
markdown scratch buffer:  wrap=true linebreak=false conceallevel=0 spell=false textwidth=0 foldmethod=manual
louiselm transcript:      wrap=true linebreak=false conceallevel=0 spell=false textwidth=0 foldmethod=manual
```

The `FileType markdown` path sets no options at all, so the transcript lost
nothing by leaving that filetype. Combined with the single-autocmd finding
above, `cd37ab2`'s blast radius on this config is empty: one plugin detached
(image.nvim, intended), one autocmd no longer firing (`MystMarkdownFiletype`,
beneficial), and no option, keymap or highlight difference.

This is the case I expected to find a regression in. It found none, and the
reason is worth keeping: the transcript never depended on `filetype=markdown`
for anything except treesitter, which `cd37ab2` re-attaches explicitly.

Worth recording as an incidental benefit, not a defect: under the old
`filetype=markdown`, `MystMarkdownFiletype` could fire on the transcript and
override its filetype whenever the conversation contained MyST content — which,
in this repo, it routinely does. `cd37ab2` makes that impossible.

| F3 `louiselm-msg` | a stray notification in the history opened for case 4 |
| F4 `louiselm-cmr` | a real payload where every fixture was well-behaved |
| F5 `louiselm-u1r` | measuring the artifact *after* F4's fix instead of trusting the assertion |
| F6 `louiselm-qcq` | a real excerpt where the test fixture was too small |

**Why the suite missed each — the transferable part.**

Three of the six (F3, F4, F6) are the *same* gap: **fixtures are well-behaved
in exactly the dimension real data is not.** `skills_spec.lua` builds symlinks
inside a temp root, so it never sees a symlink to a Rust repo with a 2839-
directory `target/`. `transcript_spec.lua` used titles like `"Run tests"`, so
it never saw a title containing a newline — and asserted with substring
searches that cannot detect an unclosed element even in principle.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs exactly the right `diff -rq` check against a
fixture too small to produce enough CSS rules for the ordering to move. In all
three the assertion was sound and the fixture was the defect. A fixture
captured from real traffic, rather than invented, would have caught all three.

F1 is different and simpler: the gate exists, is documented, and nothing runs
it. CI does not yet enforce the gates, and the previous round had `674939b` in
scope but tested behaviour rather than running the formatter. Behavioural QA
does not substitute for a gate.

F5 is the one worth internalising. F4's fix made every assertion pass — counts
balanced, no fabricated headings, elements closed. The export was still not fit
for the pipeline that consumes it, because nothing had *measured* the result.
Verifying the assertion a fix targets is not the same as inspecting what the
fix produced.

F2 was not ours at all. Worth recording anyway: the reported symptom
("neovim crashed") was wrong, and taking it at face value would have sent the
round after a `vim.treesitter.start` call that the user's own config had
already been making for months.

**Recipe bugs, mine, all corrected in place:** `<bufnr>` left as a literal
placeholder in case 1.2; `:messages` named as the evidence channel when snacks
replaces `vim.notify` and keeps its own history; repo-root-relative paths in
case 9 given to someone standing in `blog/`; "open the built page" with no
usable way to open it. The snacks one was the expensive one — it made a passing
case look like it produced no evidence.

## Leftovers

Nothing is left undecided, but these are deliberate:

- **Four findings open by choice:** `louiselm-d7l` (needs a decision on whether
  `blog/` is in scope for the gates — it fails both), `louiselm-msg` (needs a
  decision on what "outside the root" should mean), `louiselm-qcq` (the obvious
  fix collides with an existing asserted property), `louiselm-tcb` (almost
  certainly a Ghostty bug; belongs upstream once one more `dmesg` check is run).
- **`louiselm-euj` reconfirmed for the second consecutive round** and again not
  fixed. It stays parented under `louiselm-vj0`, where it was filed. A third
  reconfirmation should come with a fix or a wontfix rather than another
  re-test.
- **Crash instrumentation left installed** in `~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc`
  (`ulimit -c unlimited` plus an nvim stderr tee), marked with `louiselm-tcb`.
  Remove when that closes. `systemd-coredump` was installed during the round.
- **Not filed as a bead, saved to agent memory instead:** live API keys are
  committed in `~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc`. The user was told and deliberately
  deferred rotation on 2026-08-20. It is not louiselm work and would distort
  this project's triage.

## Findings this round

**F2 — Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it** (`louiselm-tcb`,
P1, open investigation, likely not ours). Reported mid-round as "neovim simply
crashed". It did not. `journalctl --user` shows all three
`app-ghostty-surface-transient-*.scope` units ending within one second at
05:14:18-19, then a fresh ghostty process at 05:14:27 — eleven seconds before
Neovim was relaunched at 05:14:38. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface, so
one death closes every window; Neovim was hung up, which is why there was no
deadly-signal banner. Ruled out: Neovim crash (no `ERR` in `nvim.log`), OOM
(`oom_kill 0` in the user slice), a Ghostty panic (no trace in a journal that
holds its full lifecycle), and `cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start` — the user's
config already ran `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so treesitter load
on that buffer is unchanged by the commit. Still open: the kernel log for an
AMDGPU reset, and whether image.nvim's kitty-graphics traffic is involved —
**which makes case 1.2 the discriminator, so run it.** Found by the tester when
the editor vanished, not by any case in this plan.

**F6 — `render-post` fragments are not byte-identical across runs**
(`louiselm-qcq`, P3, not fixed). `render-post.sh`'s header promises fragment
output is "a pure function of the current input" and that "running twice
against unchanged input is byte-identical". Ten consecutive runs on identical
input in an identical environment produced **four distinct fragments**; holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it, so it is run-to-run nondeterminism, not
environment sensitivity. The entire diff is CSS rule order and property order
within a rule (`.-conceal {}` moving position;
`.-markup-strong {color: …; font-weight: bold}` vs the reverse) — the `<pre>`
is identical every time and every variant renders the same, which is why case 7
looked fine. Origin is upstream: `:TOhtml` emits its `<style>` block from an
unordered table, and this pipeline preserves it verbatim by design.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs precisely the right check (`diff -rq` across
two runs) and passes anyway, because its fixture excerpts are 4–5 lines of
prose and a three-line Lua snippet — too few highlight groups for the order to
move. The real excerpt produces 11 rules. Not fixed because the obvious fix
(sort the CSS in `render-post.mjs`) collides with part 1's assertion that the
fragment matches an *independent* TOhtml capture byte-for-byte; that is a
design decision, written up in the bead.

**F5 — Single-line captions run to thousands of characters** (`louiselm-u1r`,
P2, **fixed in `3d6557d`**, closed). Exposed by F4's own fix: once captions
were one line, the longest in the verified export was **7319 characters** (then
6963, 6490) — whole `br create --description` invocations with the bead body
inlined. Correct but useless as a label, and a live risk to case 7, which
renders these exports through `:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme
fixes and does not expose. Bounded at 120 characters via
`strchars`/`strcharpart` rather than `string.sub`, since real titles carry em
dashes and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8 mid-character; the full
title is untouched in the `<details>` payload. Worth noting how this was found:
not by a case, but by measuring the artifact after a fix instead of declaring
victory on the assertion that the fix targeted.

**F4 — Multi-line tool titles break the export's `<sub>` caption and inject
fake `##` sections** (`louiselm-cmr`, P1, **fixed in `a6484ea`**, closed,
**verified** by re-export: 156 `## Tool` / 56 `## Assistant` / 17 `## User` and
no other `##`; 156 of 156 captions closing on their own line; zero multi-line
spans). Found by
case 5, and exactly the failure class the case was written for: fixtures use
short single-line titles, real payloads carry whole shell commands. In a 120
tool-call export, 12 captions span more than one line — the worst runs 150
lines — because `transcript.lua:182` interpolates `raw.title` into a
single-line string and `split_lines` then turns its embedded newlines into real
breaks. Everything between the unclosed `<sub>` and its `</sub>` lands in the
document as raw markdown, which added 28 fabricated `##` headings
(`## Observed`, `## Root cause`, …) leaked out of heredoc bead descriptions.
Older than `14dbab6` — the previous `## Tool: <title>` format split the heading
the same way — but the round found it while testing that commit. What passed:
the block counts balance exactly (120 `## Tool` / `<details>` / `<summary>` /
`</details>`), no title fell back to a raw tool id, and all statuses are real
(`completed` ×104, `failed` ×4).

**F3 — Skill discovery warns per symlinked subdirectory and scans whole source
repos** (`louiselm-msg`, P2, not fixed — out of scope). Surfaced by accident:
the snacks notifier history opened for case 4 also held
`louiselm: skill discovery found 31 issue(s)`. Thirty of those 31 are the same
"symlink resolves outside configured root" warning, fired once per symlinked
subdirectory on a stow layout where every skill is a symlink by design. The
check at `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:209` warns and then queues the
directory anyway, so it prevents nothing — and because `bvr`'s skill directory
symlinks to a whole Rust repo, discovery walks 3133 directories of which 2839
are `target/`. Measured in-process against the real config: `discover()` takes
381 ms, of which the `bvr` subtree alone accounts for 376 ms. `skills_spec.lua`
misses it because its fixtures build symlinks inside a temp root, so no case
models a symlink to a large real repository. Not fixed: nothing in
`ec19281..HEAD` touches skills, and the fix is a behavioural decision about
what "outside the root" should mean.

**F1 — `stylua --check .` fails on a clean tree** (`louiselm-d7l`, not fixed).
`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is not StyLua-formatted (single-quoted strings
where the repo config sets `quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`), so the gate
AGENTS.md §4 declares — `stylua --check .`, unscoped, whole repo — has exited 1
since `674939b`. Introduced by the blog pipeline commit, which the previous
round (`louiselm-vj0`) had in scope and did not catch, because that round tested
the pipeline's behaviour and never ran the formatter gate. Not fixed during the
round: it is a one-command fix, but it is out of scope for the cases below and
touching the tree mid-round invalidates case 0's clean-tree premise.
close_reason:
Round complete: all ten cases were run on 2026-08-20 and all six findings are now closed (louiselm-d7l, louiselm-tcb, louiselm-msg, louiselm-cmr, louiselm-u1r, louiselm-qcq). The last one, louiselm-qcq, was fixed in this session; rollup reads 6 closed, 0 open.

The round's durable record is this issue's description, per louiselm-ri1 -- the working file it was written in was deleted at close and not committed.

Two leftovers survive this issue and are tracked elsewhere:
- louiselm-euj (LouiselmToMarkdown prompts before validating an explicit session id) was reconfirmed for a second consecutive round and remains parented under louiselm-vj0, where it was filed. Per the round's own note, a third reconfirmation should come with a fix or a wontfix rather than another re-test.
- The crash instrumentation the round installed in ~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc (ulimit -c unlimited plus an nvim stderr tee) was to be removed when louiselm-tcb closed. louiselm-tcb is now closed, so that removal is outstanding. It is in a different repository, so it is not actioned here.

title: Grill-me needed: how should qa-review rounds be archived, and does beads belong in the loop
description:
Not actionable as-is — this is a seed for a future grill-me session, not a
spec to implement from. Surfaced at the close of the transcript-export/
blog-publishing QA round (2026-08-18), when a process question came up that
didn't fit anywhere in the existing skill chain.

## The open questions

- **Archiving authority.** Once a qa-review round closes, does the working
  file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) become the durable record of what was tested
  and found, or is it disposable scratch once findings are filed to beads?
  Right now nothing says either way, so rounds just accumulate as loose
  untracked files.
- **Where archiving sits in the qa-review process.** Should the qa-review
  skill itself have a defined "closing" step that decides what happens to
  the file (commit it, summarize it into beads, delete it), or is that
  always a manual call by whoever's running the round?
- **Could beads be leveraged more directly.** Instead of (or alongside) a
  markdown working file, could a qa-review round's cases/results live in
  beads itself — e.g. as a parent issue with the plan, sub-issues per case?
  Unclear if that's better or just adds ceremony to something that works
  fine as a file today.

## Why this doesn't fit the usual chain

Their standing workflow is grill-me -> to-beads -> tasks executed across
sessions ("skill chaining"). Within a qa-review round, a code bug correctly
triggers to-beads-bug — that chain already works. But this round produced a
different kind of finding: not a bug, a question about the skills/workflow
itself. There's currently no formalized way for a skill to route that kind
of self-reflective finding anywhere — it only survived this time because the
user happened to notice and say it was worth a grill-me session. Whether
findings like this should sometimes get folded directly into a skill's own
instructions (when concrete enough) versus always deferred to a grill-me
session (when still vague) is itself part of what's open here.

## A concrete proposal already on record

This question isn't new — the user raised it explicitly at the *start* of
this same QA round, in an earlier session (`claude/85f97534-8fa6-4d95-a05a-7c0851bec937`):
"while we do this i want you to think if those reviews conversation or
document you produce as part of the review could leverage beads for
historical / archiving purposes." That session's assistant answered with a
concrete sketch the user liked and wants preserved verbatim here for the
grill-me session to react to, not re-derive:

1. **One bead per round**, type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file QA_REVIEW.md`. The whole plan lands in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is committed — so the round becomes
   greppable history instead of an untracked file you have to decide about
   at the end. That's the exact question that ended the *previous* round
   (the permissions round) unresolved too: "commit it as a record, or
   delete it."
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>` — the graph then answers "which round found this?" and `br
   graph` shows a round's blast radius. This round's findings
   (`louiselm-dim`, `louiselm-euj`, `louiselm-d2o`, `louiselm-xrf`) are
   already beads but orphaned from the round that produced them — exactly
   the gap this proposal closes.
3. **Round-by-round narration goes in `br comments add`** — append-only and
   timestamped, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit). The
   markdown file stays the live scratchpad *during* the round since it
   churns every round; beads takes the final state on close.
4. **`--external-ref` holds the session id** (e.g.
   `claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384` for this round), which
   dovetails with the user's global commit-message rule (`Refs <id>` for
   named sessions/issues), and `br orphans` catches anything referenced in a
   commit but still open.

The convergence the prior session flagged as the nice part: the
transcript-export feature this very round was testing turns a session into
a publishable artifact. So under this proposal the bead becomes the index,
the exported transcript is the evidence, and a blog post (via the same
publishing pipeline, once `louiselm-xrf` is fixed) is the human-readable
version of the same round — three layers of the same feature set reused for
QA's own record-keeping instead of a fourth bespoke mechanism.

## Bigger context

Connects to a broader, previously-discussed wish: the user's own workflow
(grill-me/beads/session-chaining) eventually being expressible as a
configurable part of louiselm itself, not just a convention they follow by
hand. Not fully re-litigated here — worth pulling that thread in the
grill-me session too.

## Not covered

No decision on the concrete proposal above — it was well-received when
sketched, but never evaluated against the three open questions or actually
tried on a round (this round still used a plain `QA_REVIEW.md`). Left for
the grill-me session: whether to adopt it as-is, adapt it, or reject it in
favor of something else.
close_reason: Resolved via grill-me. Routed to feature louiselm-ri1 (Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads), with child tasks louiselm-ri1.1 (skill closing step) and louiselm-ri1.2 (retroactive close of QA_REVIEW.md and QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md, blocked on ri1.1). Adopted the concrete proposal on record as-is: one chore/qa-round bead per round via --description-file + --external-ref, findings as children via the existing to-beads-bug chain, cases stay flat (never beaded), narration via br comments, working file deleted on close. Bigger workflow-config-engine thread explicitly left out of scope per agreement.

title: Skill/file/buffer/selection context pickers are unreachable through the documented :LouiselmChat setup path
description:
The chat context-queuing API (`pick_skill`, `pick_file`, `mention_buffer`, `send_selection`) documented in README.md under "Chat context" is completely unreachable through the plugin's own documented setup path, so no user who follows the README can ever attach a file, skill, buffer mention, or visual selection to a prompt.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 while setting up a manual QA round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP skill invocation): asked the user to invoke the skill picker to test it, and they had never wired anything for it -- because there is nothing to wire it to.

`grep -rn "pick_skill\|pick_file\|mention_buffer\|send_selection" lua/ --include="*.lua" | grep -v chat/init.lua` returns nothing: these four `Chat` methods are defined in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and never called anywhere else in the tree -- not in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua (which backs `:LouiselmChat` and every other registered `:Louiselm*` command), not anywhere.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` registers 12 `:Louiselm*` ex commands (LouiselmChat, LouiselmNewSession, LouiselmResume, LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmRenameSession, LouiselmSessionId, LouiselmToMarkdown, LouiselmCloseSession, LouiselmCancel, LouiselmSessionOptions, LouiselmPermissions, LouiselmInline) -- none of them calls pick_skill/pick_file/mention_buffer/send_selection.

The `chat` object these methods live on is a local upvalue private to `Command.register()`'s closure (command.lua:194 `local chat`); nothing exposes it, and `Louiselm.setup()` (lua/louiselm/init.lua) returns only a boolean. So even a user willing to write their own keymap has no object to call these methods on unless they bypass `Louiselm.setup()`/`:LouiselmChat` entirely and hand-construct a second, parallel `Chat` instance via the low-level `require("louiselm.ui.chat").new(sessions, {...})` constructor -- which would not be attached to the same session as their real chat buffer.

README.md documents these four methods under "## Chat context" (around line 438) as plain Lua snippets (`chat:mention_buffer()`, `chat:send_selection()`, `chat:pick_file()`, `chat:pick_skill()`) with no indication that `chat` here is a user-constructed low-level object, not the one `:LouiselmChat` creates -- reading the README top to bottom gives no working path to ever call them.

## Symptoms

- Following the README exactly (`Louiselm.setup(config)` + `:LouiselmChat`), there is no command, keymap, or other UI affordance to pick a skill, pick a file, mention the source buffer, or send a visual selection.
- The entire native/inject skill-invocation feature (including the just-shipped louiselm-2w4) is unreachable in practice for the documented setup path.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua never registers commands for these four `Chat` methods, and never exposes the `chat` instance it privately constructs.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/context_spec.lua` call `chat:pick_skill()` etc. directly on a `Chat` object constructed in the test, which is exactly the low-level path the README also (accidentally) documents -- so the tests exercise the methods correctly but never assert that the *shipped, documented, high-level setup path* (`:LouiselmChat`) can reach them. No test covers `command.lua`'s command surface for context actions because there was never a command to cover.

## Fix direction

Add `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile` (optional root arg, `nargs = "?"`, mirroring `:LouiselmToMarkdown`'s optional-arg pattern), `:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, and `:LouiselmSendSelection` to command.lua, following the existing `if chat == nil then report_error("no chat session is open") ... end` pattern used by `:LouiselmCancel`/`:LouiselmSessionOptions`/`:LouiselmCloseSession` (these need an already-open session to queue context onto, unlike `:LouiselmChat`/`:LouiselmPermissions` which use `ensure_chat()` to open one on demand). Update README's command list (around line 269) and the "Chat context" section to stop implying the low-level constructor snippet is reachable from the documented setup path.

## Acceptance

- New `:Louiselm*` commands registered and covered by a test in tests/ui/command_spec.lua that drives them through the real `:LouiselmChat` + `Command.register()` path (matching the file's existing "through the normal chat path" test style), not just calling the Chat method directly.
- README updated to list the new commands and no longer implies the raw snippets are usable from a documented setup.

## Not covered

- Whether default keymaps (not just ex commands) are also warranted -- left as a separate decision; this bug is about there being no path at all, not about ergonomics beyond a command existing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e553a1. Added :LouiselmPickSkill, :LouiselmPickFile [root], :LouiselmMentionBuffer, :LouiselmSendSelection to lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua, matching the existing chat==nil guard pattern used by :LouiselmCancel/:LouiselmSessionOptions. Tests: command existence check, a combined 'no chat session is open' case for all four, and a real end-to-end test driving :LouiselmMentionBuffer through :LouiselmChat + a fake ACP process, asserting the chip renders and the queued context is sent in the next session/prompt. Updated README's command list and Chat context section. Gates: full mini.test suite green, stylua and lua-language-server clean repo-wide (excluding a pre-existing unrelated blog/ script). Deferred: default keymaps beyond the ex commands, per the bead's own 'Not covered' note.

title: Investigate default availability of LouiselmResume
description:
## Goal

Determine whether the new `:LouiselmResume` command is available for a normal louiselm.nvim installation using the user configuration in `~/.config/nvim`, and make it available by default if it is not.

## Evidence

The previous commit `798712b` added `LouiselmResume` registration inside `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`, but registration appears to depend on an explicit `require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").register()` call. The repository test and manual init files call this explicitly; verify whether the production plugin entrypoint does so for ordinary Neovim startup.

## Scope

- Reproduce/check command availability from the normal plugin runtime path and from the user configuration path.
- Trace plugin load order and setup behavior, including whether `louiselm.setup()` is required before the command exists.
- If missing by default, add the narrowest production registration fix and update/extend headless behavioral coverage and documentation as needed.
- Preserve explicit configuration behavior and avoid duplicate-registration side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The task records the observed behavior and root cause for a normal installation.
2. `:LouiselmResume` and `:LouiselmResume!` are available after ordinary plugin loading, without requiring users to manually require/register the command.
3. Existing command registration remains repeatable and tests cover the production startup path.
4. Focused tests, the full mini.test suite, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks are run or their unavailability is reported.
close_reason: Registered all chat commands from successful louiselm.setup(), added a regression test proving LouiselmResume and bang support are available after setup, and updated README wording. Verification: focused setup test passed; full mini.test suite passed (126 cases, with swap files directed to /tmp); stylua --check passed; lua-language-server --check passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Inline human-readable rendering for jsonl log lines
description:
Idea from conversation, not yet designed: for jsonl files, render each line's *display* as a compact human-readable string (e.g. "14:23:05 WRN nvim.175374 server_start:197 Failed to start server...") via conceal/virtual-text, without touching the underlying buffer content — the file stays true jsonl on disk (greppable/diffable/pipeable).

Context: jsonl.nvim already renders jsonl nicely via treesitter formatting. jsonlogs.nvim takes a different approach — splitting into an expanded pretty-printed panel/view — which trades away the one-line-per-record structure that makes jsonl useful in the first place. That's judged as doing too much for the goal here.

Closer prior art: render-markdown.nvim's approach of decorating a buffer's *display* without mutating its content. Worth checking whether treesitter's line-level virtual text/decoration hooks, or the same conceal machinery jsonl.nvim already uses, can drive this before reaching for a new plugin/dependency.

Not yet scoped as an implementation task — needs design: what subset of jsonl schemas to target (arbitrary vs known log formats), how much configurability, conflict with existing jsonl.nvim formatting.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Implemented as lua/louiselm/forensics/{log_view.lua,command.lua} + :LouiselmForensicsLogView.

Confirmed target: acp-llm-adapter/acp-proxy stdout-jsonrpc.log files under
~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter -- real JSON-RPC 2.0 ACP traffic, one message
per line. Design landed on Neovim's native fold machinery instead of extmark
overlay: foldexpr forces one fold per line, foldtext renders a compact human
summary (dispatches on session/update's sessionUpdate kind, reusing the same
kind vocabulary session/lifecycle.lua already handles), buffer content is
never touched, zo/zO reveals the exact raw line. Reuses acp/protocol.lua's
decode/validate rather than re-parsing JSON-RPC.

Verified live against a real 1051-line log: all lines fold/render, widths
stay bounded, zero errors.

Known limitation, not fixed here: streamed text arrives as one JSON-RPC line
per small delta, so a paragraph of agent_message_chunk/agent_thought_chunk
becomes many one-or-two-word folds rather than one merged block. Fixing that
means multi-line folds keyed on messageId -- a materially bigger feature than
this one-line-to-one-fold v1. Left as a possible follow-up, not filed as a
separate issue yet pending user reaction to v1.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Follow-up from live testing: za felt sluggish, and a request to keep this
free of regex.

Regex removed: the only pattern-matching in the file was single_line's gsub
collapsing embedded newlines for display; replaced with plain (non-pattern)
vim.split/table.concat/vim.trim. JSON parsing itself was never regex -- it
already went through vim.json.decode via acp/protocol.lua.

Investigated delegating fold *boundaries* to the already-installed jsonl/json
treesitter fold query instead of the hand-rolled foldexpr, per the instinct
that hand-rolling is redundant when a treesitter parser is already there.
Tested directly: wired foldexpr to vim.treesitter.foldexpr() against a real
log and foldlevel() came back 0 for every line. Root cause: every ACP
JSON-RPC record is exactly one physical line, and Neovim's/Vim's fold model
only ever folds a node whose start and end line differ -- a same-line node
never registers as a fold, treesitter or not. There's no existing
one-fold-per-line building block to delegate to for this shape; forcing a
fold boundary at every line via a custom foldexpr remains the only way to
get it. Documented this finding in the module's doc comment so it isn't
re-litigated later.

Real fix for the sluggishness: foldtext had zero caching -- it re-decoded
and re-summarized the raw line from scratch on every redraw of every visible
closed fold. Added a per-buffer, per-line cache keyed against the exact raw
line text (self-invalidating on edit, no changedtick bookkeeping needed).
Added a test that spies on render_line to prove a repeated foldtextresult()
call for an unchanged line hits the cache instead of re-rendering.

Caveat: benchmarked the fix against the real 1051-line log used earlier
(lines up to 55KB) and could not reproduce dramatic sluggishness even before
this fix -- full-buffer foldtextresult sweep ~26ms, 50x za ~1ms in headless
timing. So either this fix already resolves what was felt live, or the

title: Usage telemetry is unreadable when flush against transcript content
description:
The chat transcript renders the `[usage] ...` line without a blank line above or below it, making usage telemetry hard to read when it is adjacent to prose or tool output. Add vertical spacing around the usage line, following the existing transcript block-spacing precedent used for tools and terminal completion.

## Observed

Seen in the maintainer screenshot on 2026-08-25 at 17:13 local time (Europe/Paris), Neovim chat buffer in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260825_1713_1920x1200_1787670818.png`

The visible transcript contains:

```text
Recorded all of this as a comment on **louiselm-exw0** and committed (`5dd00ba`). Ready to tackle the implementation when you are.
[usage] total_tokens=3468175 · input_tokens=...
> i just asked in codex for reason but it showed nothing ...
```

The usage row is directly adjacent to the preceding and following transcript content, with no empty line separating it.

## Symptoms

- Human-facing chat transcript usage telemetry is difficult to scan.
- Usage should be presented as its own block with one newline above and below.

## Root cause

Likely in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2250-2263`: the `turn_done` handler calls `insert_transcript(self, view, { line })` for the usage line, but does not surround it with empty lines. The neighboring terminal-completion path explicitly inserts blank lines, which suggests the usage path omitted equivalent block spacing. This mechanism is a hypothesis based on the current source and screenshot; verify with a focused UI regression test.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover usage formatting and transcript ordering/data, but no headless UI assertion currently requires blank lines around the rendered usage line in the live chat transcript.

## Fix direction

At the transcript presentation boundary in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, insert one empty line before and after the usage line while preserving existing behavior for turns without usage and avoiding duplicate blank lines where the preceding/following block already supplies spacing. Add a behavioral headless regression test for the rendered transcript.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- In the chat buffer, `[usage] ...` has exactly one blank line above and below it, including when adjacent to prose or tool output.
- Usage formatting and persistence remain unchanged.

## Not covered

The screenshot does not establish whether every usage-producing agent or replay path has the same spacing issue. Verify live and replay rendering when implementing the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree. Root cause was usage presentation inserting only the usage line, unlike neighboring transcript blocks with explicit separators. Added neighbor-aware spacing for live and replay usage. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 117/117; full MiniTest suite 517/517. Gates: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems. Acceptance met: usage is separated from surrounding transcript content.
