title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm formalize a persisted project vocabulary from grill-me sessions
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as explicit "food for thought" on 2026-08-20. Originally noted only in
an agent's private memory; migrated into beads on 2026-08-20 alongside
louiselm-3od once it was pointed out that louiselm is cross-adapter by
design, so a note only one adapter can see is exactly the kind of context
AGENTS.md says does not belong there.

## The question

Should louiselm (or its workflow) formalize a persisted "project vocabulary" --
a working glossary that accumulates meaning from `grill-me` sessions over
time, so each term embeds context that would otherwise need re-explaining --
and if so, what does that mechanism look like here?

## Context

The user referenced a video by mattpocock (the original author of the
`grill-me` skill/pattern) describing that a grill-me session's real product
is shared understanding, and that over time this naturally produces a working
vocabulary for a project. The user recalled mattpocock built this into one of
his own skills: a mechanism that persists the accumulated vocabulary to a
markdown file rather than letting it live only in conversation history. The
user wants something equivalent for their own workflow here, and floated
possibly integrating it with beads -- the local issue tracker this project
already leans on heavily (`br`/`bvr` triage, the `to-beads-*` skill family).

## Threads worth pulling

- Whether this lives as its own artifact (a `VOCABULARY.md` or similar) or as
  structured beads content (e.g. a dedicated issue type, or metadata on
  existing issues).
- How it interacts with the `to-beads-*` skill family, which already turns
  grill-me sessions into beads work -- is vocabulary a byproduct of that
  same pipeline, or a separate one?
- Two concrete instances of the problem this would solve already exist in
  this project. First, "chat" vs. "session" naming drift (caught and
  corrected once, but only recorded in an agent's private memory before this
  migration). Second, and far more expensive, "model" vs. "provider" on
  2026-08-21 -- see the worked example below. A persisted vocabulary
  mechanism would presumably have caught or prevented both on its own.
- Worth checking mattpocock's public work (skills, videos, blog) for the
  specific mechanism he built, if the user references it again, rather than
  reinventing it blind.
- Related, separately filed thread: louiselm-3od (documentation strategy) --
  not the same question, but a persisted vocabulary could plausibly feed or
  overlap with an agent-legible documentation artifact. Worth deciding during
  either grill whether they should be one session or two.

## Worked example: "model" vs. "provider" (2026-08-21)

The maintainer asked whether `:LouiselmModelChange` should exist, then said
"file it as a priority beads task and implement it asap". An agent filed
louiselm-model-change-cl59, implemented it test-first, passed all three gates,
and committed it (1e7e560). The maintainer then clarified that by "model" they
had meant *provider*: switching a live Claude session to Codex, not switching
between the models one agent advertises. The commit was reverted (db39f96) and
the bead closed as not planned.

What makes this the strongest available argument for the mechanism:

- The ambiguity was invisible to both parties. The agent checked the code,
  confirmed the capability already existed, cited the tests covering it, and
  was told to proceed. Nothing in the exchange surfaced that the two sides
  were pointing at different referents.
- The cost was not an argument about naming. It was a wrong feature built,
  reviewed, gated, committed to main, and reverted.
- The two referents are not near-synonyms wearing different labels. A model
  change is one `session/set_config_option` call inside a live ACP session; a
  provider change needs a different agent process, a different connection,
  and a different session, so the current session cannot survive it. A
  glossary entry binding each term to its definition would have made the
  mismatch visible at the moment the command was proposed.
- ACP already supplies the disambiguating vocabulary: the option carries
  `category = "model"`, while the agent is a separately configured definition.
  A project vocabulary would have had a wire-level authority to anchor to
  rather than inventing a house convention.

Note for the grill: this example argues the vocabulary has to be legible at
*proposal* time, not only at review time. A VOCABULARY.md that nobody reads
before implementing would not have prevented this. That is a constraint on the
mechanism, not just on the artifact.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.
close_reason: Resolved through grill-me: confirmed a Beads-native vocabulary lifecycle, promoted Agent/Model/Session/Handoff/Provider reference records, and created feature louiselm-ce6.22 with implementation tasks louiselm-ce6.22.1 and louiselm-ce6.22.2.

comments.author: claude/cca6e4b5-ff23-495e-a84c-6a69b4c18c99
comments.text: Cross-reference: louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs is the real want that the model/provider slip was hiding. If the vocabulary grill runs first, 'provider' vs 'model' is a ready-made first entry with a wire-level authority (ACP category) to anchor to.

comments.author: claude/cca6e4b5-ff23-495e-a84c-6a69b4c18c99
comments.text: Second vocabulary candidate, from the 2026-08-21 grill on louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs: the `needs-capability:*` label namespace agreed in louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc is a controlled vocabulary by construction, and it already has a live drift risk -- `multimodal` exists on louiselm-ce6.21 and overlaps semantically with an image-generation capability name. Two properties make it a useful test case for whatever this grill decides. It is greppable (`br label list-all | grep needs-capability:`), so the vocabulary has a mechanical inventory rather than a prose one; and `br label rename` rewrites a label across every issue, so a bad entry is repairable rather than permanent. If the vocabulary mechanism cannot express 'these two names mean the same thing, prefer this one', it will not survive contact with this namespace.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 1 — ambiguity handling is consequence-based. If competing meanings imply materially different architecture, lifecycle, protocol behavior, authority, or user-visible behavior, stop before implementation and require explicit confirmation. Harmless naming drift may be silently normalized to the canonical term. The gate is therefore not every unknown word; it is ambiguity whose interpretations would produce meaningfully different work.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text:
Research note — upstream and Beads capabilities (2026-08-23). Matt Pocock's current upstream separates plain grill-me (delegates only to grilling) from grill-with-docs (composes grilling + domain-modeling). domain-modeling updates CONTEXT.md inline as terms crystallize, keeps it glossary-only and implementation-free, lists avoided synonyms, checks ambiguous terms against code, and relies on repo instructions to make later skills read/use it. Upstream to-tickets consumes that glossary but the tracker is not its canonical vocabulary store. Sources: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/main/README.md; /skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md; /skills/engineering/domain-modeling/SKILL.md; /skills/engineering/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md.

Local divergence: this repo's grill-me waits for shared understanding and then invokes to-beads; local to-beads requires project vocabulary in outputs but does not create or maintain a vocabulary artifact.

Beads 0.4.0 can support a Beads-native glossary: custom issue types are accepted (a dry-run with type=vocabulary succeeded); list/search filter by type/status/label; search covers title, description, id, and comments; descriptions are replaceable; comments retain rationale; saved queries and git-backed JSONL provide discovery/history. A closed vocabulary reference is excluded from ready work. Important limits: Beads does not ambiently inject the glossary before proposal work; AGENTS/skills must explicitly load it. One bead per term would inflate issue/closure/velocity metrics and fragment the glossary. agent_context inheritance follows parent hierarchy, so using it project-wide would corrupt product hierarchy. Strong candidate: one closed custom-type vocabulary bead per bounded context, with canonical current definitions in its description, rationale/history in comments, and separate open question beads for disputed changes; AGENTS and grill/to-beads load it before proposing work.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 2 — use Beads as the canonical vocabulary store. The storage unit is one closed custom-type  bead per bounded context, starting with one project-wide LouiseLM vocabulary bead. Its description is the current concise glossary; comments preserve rationale/history; open question beads carry disputed or proposed changes. Do not create one bead per term, which would fragment consumption and distort tracker metrics.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Correction to comment 169: the omitted custom issue type is vocabulary. Agreement 2 is unchanged: use one closed vocabulary bead per bounded context, starting with one project-wide LouiseLM vocabulary bead. Its description is the current concise glossary; comments preserve rationale/history; open question beads carry disputed or proposed changes. Do not create one bead per term.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 3 — load vocabulary at grill start, keep term decisions provisional on the source question during discussion, and promote resolved terms to the canonical vocabulary bead only after the user confirms shared understanding. Promotion happens even when no implementation work results. Adoption constraint still to settle: the first run and later grills must not trigger a retroactive vocabulary audit or flood the workflow with terminology disputes.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 4 — vocabulary adoption is an incremental ratchet, not a migration. Do not scan repository history or the backlog for terms, do not treat missing entries as debt or warnings, and do not pursue completeness. Seed only proven high-cost distinctions. A grill proposes vocabulary changes only when ambiguity materially affects its current decision; harmless synonyms do not trigger discussion. A comprehensive vocabulary audit requires an explicit user request.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Tradeoff analysis for universal loading. Costs: a small process and context tax on every applicable session; irrelevant vocabulary if bounded contexts multiply; stale definitions can steer agents confidently away from current code; custom vocabulary issues still appear in aggregate tracker metrics; a Beads JSONL issue is one record, so concurrent edits to one vocabulary description have coarser merge behavior than line-oriented Markdown; and two sessions that both read then replace the description can produce a semantic last-writer-wins loss even though SQLite serializes each write. Guardrails: load once only for sessions that plan, implement, review, or file work, not pure housekeeping; keep definitions conceptual, short, and free of countable implementation facts; load only relevant contexts once multiple contexts exist; keep canonical vocabulary beads closed so they never enter ready scheduling; re-read immediately before promotion and refuse or reconcile when updated_at changed; route disagreements through question beads rather than reopening the vocabulary reference.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 5 — vocabulary loading is mandatory once per semantic work session: planning, implementation, review, or filing work. Pure housekeeping and mechanical changes may skip it. Load only relevant bounded contexts, keep entries concise and conceptual, keep canonical vocabulary beads closed, and re-read updated_at immediately before promotion to detect concurrent change. Expected context cost is intentionally small because the vocabulary is not expected or encouraged to become exhaustive.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 6 — semantic freshness is conflict-driven, not periodically audited. SQLite and JSONL provide durable current storage but cannot determine whether a definition still matches product intent or code. When vocabulary, code, a work item, or user intent materially contradict one another, neither source automatically wins. Stop, create or reuse a vocabulary question bead, resolve the conflict with the user, then promote the agreed definition to the canonical vocabulary bead.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 7 — implement vocabulary as workflow infrastructure first, not as a louiselm.nvim runtime subsystem. Initial scope is a canonical Beads vocabulary bead, project instructions for loading and conflicts, and local grill-me/to-beads integration for consumption and end-of-grill promotion. Dogfood several real grills before considering any plugin command or UI; productize only from observed workflow friction.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 8 — seed only the proven high-value language from the model/provider failure and shipped handoff. Canonical concepts: Agent is a named configured ACP entry LouiseLM can start sessions with; Model is an agent-advertised option that can change within the same session; Session is a conversation bound to one agent and cannot change agents; Handoff creates a session with another agent, injects a reviewed transcript, and retains the source session. Provider is reserved for the underlying vendor or service and is avoided when referring to a configured agent entry.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Format investigation revises the earlier storage recommendation. In an isolated Beads workspace, a custom type vocabulary bead with custom status reference was accepted. br list filtered by type/status with TOON exposed title, description, design, and notes as distinct fields; normal br show rendered the same fields readably. BVR ignored the reference-status bead entirely: it was absent from total/type/status counts, recommendations, and actionable work. A single vocabulary bead using agent_context was less suitable because br emits agent_context as a JSON-encoded string and a human view would require a duplicated rendering. Strong revised candidate: one reference-status vocabulary bead per canonical term; title=term, description=one or two sentence definition, notes=Avoid and Distinguish-from guidance, design=provenance/source question. Query all terms in one TOON call. This is genuinely Beads-structured, avoids one opaque multi-term description, isolates concurrent updates per term, remains human-readable, and does not pollute BVR work metrics.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 9 supersedes agreement 2 storage granularity. Use one Beads record per canonical term, with issue_type=vocabulary and status=reference. Title is the canonical term; description is its tight conceptual definition; notes carry Avoid and Distinguish-from guidance; design carries current provenance/source questions. Agents load all applicable terms with br list filtered by vocabulary/reference in TOON format; humans inspect the same records with br show. Add context labels only when multiple bounded contexts actually emerge. Isolated verification proved reference records are excluded from br ready and from BVR project counts, recommendations, and graph analysis.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 10 — the final shared-understanding summary must include an explicit compact vocabulary delta: terms to create, terms to update with the semantic change, or no vocabulary changes. The user confirmation of that single final summary authorizes both vocabulary promotion and creation/update of resulting work items. Do not mutate vocabulary silently, and do not add a second confirmation ceremony after shared understanding.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Agreement 11 — grill-me behavior replacement and bootstrap: supersedes the proposed opt-in-by-existing-vocabulary-record behavior discussed in the transcript. Do not introduce a separately named grill-me-vocabulary command. Keep the grill-me name and change its standard behavior so every grill-me session performs the vocabulary workflow: load any existing vocabulary/reference records, treat an empty result as a valid first-session state, surface a vocabulary delta in the shared-understanding summary, and create the first vocabulary records after confirmation. Existing vocabulary records are not an activation flag.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Agreement 12 — projects without Beads: grill-me remains usable when the current project has no Beads database, but explicitly reports that the vocabulary delta cannot be persisted. It must not silently initialize Beads. In a Beads-enabled project, zero vocabulary/reference records is a valid bootstrap state and does not disable the vocabulary workflow.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Implementation refinement from the confirmed bootstrap: br list rejects an undeclared custom status when no reference record exists, while br list --type vocabulary --status all --format toon returns a structured empty result. Therefore discovery must query vocabulary across statuses and consume only records whose status is reference. This preserves the agreed vocabulary/reference invariant without silently editing project policy or breaking first use.

title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm adopt or integrate a sandboxed execution environment such as nono?
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

## Question

How should louiselm think about sandboxed execution environments for agents, and should it evaluate or integrate a provider such as nono rather than treating sandboxing only as an abstract capability in its own policy model?

## Trigger and sources

A pull request discussion mentioned [nono](https://nono.sh/docs/core/overview), whose Rust core library exposes capability-based filesystem/network controls, OS-level enforcement via Landlock on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS, and C FFI. The project homepage describes it as created by the team behind Sigstore; the relationship should be verified rather than assumed to mean that nono has Sigstore project governance or guarantees.

- nono core overview: https://nono.sh/docs/core/overview
- nono project: https://nono.sh/
- nono source: https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono
- Existing louiselm security feature: `louiselm-qbr.5.1` (capability envelopes and verified isolation)

## Threads worth pulling

- Compare nono with the existing generic isolation model: what can be represented as an attested enforcement boundary, and what remains provider-specific?
- Decide whether louiselm should integrate a Rust/FFI sandbox, launch agents through an external sandbox, define a provider-neutral adapter, or keep sandboxing outside louiselm. Do not add an abstraction merely because one implementation exists.
- Examine whether process-level Landlock/Seatbelt confinement is sufficient for louiselm’s threat model, especially network mediation, credentials/phantom-token patterns, subprocess inheritance, writable workspaces, `/tmp`, symlinks, and host-side tools.
- Determine the minimum evidence required before trusting a sandbox provider: kernel/OS prerequisites, fail-closed behavior, policy coverage, escape resistance, lifecycle/cancellation behavior, auditability, version/provenance, and tests against adversarial agents.
- Clarify whether a sandbox should narrow capability authorization only, or also be required before unattended execution; preserve the principle that a sandbox is not authority by itself.
- Check project maturity, governance, security history, and maintenance before making a dependency or product commitment.

## Desired outcome

A short design decision recorded in beads answering whether sandboxed environments belong in louiselm’s trusted enforcement boundary, whether nono is a candidate worth a spike, and what concrete evidence or follow-up issue is required.

## Out of scope

Do not add a runtime dependency, Rust code, FFI, or provider integration as part of this reflection. Do not treat the “team behind Sigstore” wording as a security certification.

title: Parallel tool completions fragment chat folds
description: Observed in claude/272bb048-875f-4156-9b3f-28e7e1b85e3e and screenshot /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260823_0408_943x1122_1787450923.png: one accidental subset of a tool-call paragraph is folded while neighboring completed calls stay expanded. The raw ACP log proves three parallel calls started in visual order A/B/C but completed B/C/A. chat/init.lua records completed lines in completion-event order and requires each new line to equal run.last + 1; a non-adjacent completion closes the run, so native folds depend on callback order rather than the rendered paragraph. Existing tests emit start/finish sequentially and miss parallel out-of-order completion. Acceptance: add a failing UI regression test with parallel starts and out-of-order finishes; after a prose chunk or turn_done, all contiguous completed tool lines in the rendered paragraph are one closed native fold regardless of completion order; failed and still-active calls remain unfolded; focused/full MiniTest, StyLua, and lua-language-server gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed tool folding to use rendered paragraph order; regression and all Lua gates pass

comments.author: codex/01a02c60-cf03-7eb2-8d6b-a4faa443c9e1
comments.text: Deeper reproduction from the same raw ACP log: each tool ID emits several non-terminal tool_call/tool_call_update events (Terminal, full command, shortened command). Chat currently appends every tool_call_started event and overwrites tool_lines[id], leaving prior started rows in the same visual paragraph. Sorting final completion rows alone would still not fold the screenshot. The regression therefore models repeated started updates plus B/C/A completion and requires the complete rendered paragraph to fold.

comments.author: codex/01a02c60-cf03-7eb2-8d6b-a4faa443c9e1
comments.text: Implemented paragraph-based folding: rendered tool lines are tracked as one contiguous paragraph, latest terminal status is tracked by tool ID, and paragraph closure creates folds only across completed-status spans. This makes repeated progress rows and out-of-order B/C/A completion fold together while failed/active IDs remain visible. Red proof: focused chat suite failed at tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:514 with foldclosed(6)=-1 instead of 6. Green proof: focused chat 94/94; full MiniTest 351/351; stylua --check .; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning (zero problems); git diff --check.

title: Re-publish louiselm GitLab repo once licence is cleared

title: Picker view shows only one visible entry despite multiple items
description:
## Summary

The picker view appears to contain only one visible entry, although its item count indicates that multiple items are available.

## Expected behavior

The picker should render enough of its list content for the available entries to be visibly distinguishable, with normal scrolling/navigation exposing the remaining items.

## Actual behavior

The view looks as if it has only one entry. The picker reports more items than are visibly displayed. The content rendered for an item may be too long and could be consuming the available display area.

## Ownership hypothesis

This may not be a louiselm rendering bug. Investigate whether the behavior comes from the snacks.nvim picker configuration/layout, item formatting, wrapping, height, or preview settings before changing louiselm.

## Reproduction

Open the affected louiselm picker and compare the visible entries with the picker-reported item count.

## Acceptance criteria

- Determine whether the root cause is louiselm or snacks.nvim configuration.
- If louiselm owns the issue, make multiple available entries visibly usable without breaking navigation.
- If snacks.nvim configuration owns it, document the required configuration change and avoid an unnecessary louiselm workaround.
notes: Root cause confirmed outside LouiseLM: the active Snacks configuration sets picker.win.list.wo.wrap=true globally. LouiseLM passes distinct choices through vim.ui.select; wrapped long rows consume the select layout height. README documents a picker.sources.select win.list.wo.wrap=false override, verified against the installed Snacks config merge. No provider-specific LouiseLM workaround added.
close_reason: Confirmed Snacks list wrapping as root cause and documented the source-scoped configuration fix

title: Restyle README hero with mural print aesthetic
description:
## Goal
Restyle the existing README hero so it uses the supplied mural reference visual language while preserving the current LouiseLM composition, spirit, and symbols.

## Scope
- In scope: replace `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` in place, using `/home/lotso/Downloads/1786245984429.jpg` as the visual reference.
- Preserve the existing landscape composition and recognizable motifs: the central portrait; connected mesh; people writing, coding, organizing, and speaking; the books, cubes, leaf, microphone, waveform, raised fists, megaphone, birds, and building.
- Apply a strict white, black, and red treatment: a clearer neutral or slightly warm white instead of the current beige/parchment cast; dense near-black ink; and vivid deep-red accents.
- Give the black artwork the reference mural character: rough hand-printed woodcut or engraved linework, cross-hatching and stippling, imperfect ink coverage, distressed contours, and slight registration/edge irregularity. Keep enough contrast and detail for README display size.
- Retain subtle physical surface or print texture, but do not let it muddy the white ground or read as yellowed paper.
- Out of scope: changing README copy, image placement, alt text, core composition, adding unrelated symbols, or turning the scene into a photograph of a building/mural.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` is replaced at the same path and remains a valid WebP with an approximately 2:1 landscape aspect ratio, so the existing README reference needs no change.
2. The original image narrative, layout, central figure, and listed symbols remain immediately recognizable; the work is a stylistic revision rather than a redesign.
3. The visible palette is limited to bright neutral/slightly warm white, dense black, and deep red. The dominant cream/sepia cast is gone and white areas read noticeably whiter than in the current asset.
4. Black figures and marks consistently resemble aged mural/woodcut ink: irregular, tactile, strongly hatched or stippled, and less digitally clean, without losing legibility.
5. Red remains an accent that guides the eye and does not overpower the black linework or white ground.
6. The image renders correctly from `README.md` at full size and thumbnail size, with no accidental cropping, illegible key motifs, or unrelated asset changes.

## Testing
- Open the final WebP directly and render `README.md`; inspect both full-size and typical repository-page display sizes.
- Verify the output format, dimensions/aspect ratio, and unchanged README asset path.
- Compare side by side with the existing hero and `/home/lotso/Downloads/1786245984429.jpg` against every visual acceptance criterion.

## Notes
- The reference image is a local, untracked visual source. Its relevant traits are recorded above so the task remains actionable if that file is unavailable.
- Favor a focused image edit/style transfer over regenerating the scene from scratch, because symbol and composition preservation is the primary constraint.

title: Sync now waits behind hours-long upload backoff
description:
Tapping Sync now while the unique upload chain is retrying does not make an immediate upload attempt. The new request is appended behind the backed-off work, so a user who has restored connectivity can remain stuck for hours despite explicitly asking to sync.

## Observed

Physical Android QA for louiselm-qbr.1.9 on 2026-08-21, Xiaomi 21081111RG, app 0.1.0, workstation and phone on 192.168.10.0/24.

After the user confirmed `Paired with https://192.168.10.121:7391`, tapped Sync now, and still saw `6 capture(s) waiting locally`, `adb shell dumpsys jobscheduler dev.louiselm.capture` reported:

```
Minimum latency: +3h10m0s129ms
Required constraints: TIMING_DELAY CONNECTIVITY
Satisfied constraints: CONNECTIVITY DEVICE_NOT_DOZING BACKGROUND_NOT_RESTRICTED TARE_WEALTH WITHIN_QUOTA
Unsatisfied constraints: TIMING_DELAY
```

The receiver still contained 4 captures, and none of the 6 pending phone captures gained upload state or an uploaded marker.

## Symptoms

- The user taps Sync now, but the visible waiting count remains 6.
- Android reports validated Wi-Fi connectivity but defers the worker for more than three hours.

## Root cause

`android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/UploadWorker.kt:42-50` routes every trigger through `enqueueUniqueWork(..., ExistingWorkPolicy.APPEND_OR_REPLACE, request)`. A manual request is appended behind the existing retry chain, preserving its exponential-backoff timing instead of running now.

## Why it was not caught

The Android tests cover protocol and storage behavior, but do not distinguish automatic retry scheduling from the user-initiated Sync now action or inspect unique-work policy.

## Fix direction

Separate the manual-sync scheduling policy from ordinary automatic enqueue. Manual sync should replace/cancel backed-off unique work and enqueue a connected-network request immediately; automatic capture/pair triggers should retain normal retry coalescing. Keep one upload worker and one unique-work name.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves manual sync selects an immediate replacement policy while automatic enqueue retains retry-safe coalescing.
- With a real backed-off worker and restored Wi-Fi, tapping Sync now causes an immediate receiver request.
- Pending captures upload under their original UUIDs without duplicates.

## Not covered

Automatic exponential backoff timing itself and OEM-specific WorkManager scheduling beyond the connected Xiaomi device are not changed.
close_reason: Fixed in 43aaa9b. Manual Sync now replaces backed-off unique work while automatic triggers retain retry coalescing. Regression: UploadWorkerTest.manualSyncReplacesBackedOffUploadWork failed before and passed after. Physical Xiaomi retest uploaded all six queued UUIDs immediately, raised receiver count 4 to 10, preserved each UUID, and left zero attention. Gates: Gradle test/lint/assembleDebug, 315 mini.test cases, StyLua, and lua-language-server all pass.

title: Beads inspector: :LouiselmInspectBead fails on any issue with no labels
description:
## Symptom

`:LouiselmInspectBead` (and the `<leader>lB` mapping) on a label-less issue
shows "louiselm: br returned malformed issue data" and never opens the
floating window. Only reproduces for issues that have zero labels.

## Evidence

Reported live during manual QA round while inspecting `louiselm-1yei` (just
filed, no labels). Confirmed directly:

```
$ br show louiselm-1yei --json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('labels' in json.load(sys.stdin)[0])"
False
$ br show louiselm-7rup --json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0].get('labels'))"
['qa-round']
```

`br show --json` omits the `labels` key entirely when an issue has no labels,
rather than emitting `[]`.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`, `decode_issue` (~line 51-87):

```lua
local function decode_issue(value)
  if type(value) ~= "table" or type(value[1]) ~= "table" then
    return nil
  end
  local issue = value[1]
  if
    ...
    or type(issue.labels) ~= "table"
    ...
  then
    return nil
  end
  ...
```

`issue.labels` is `nil` when `br` omits the key, so `type(issue.labels) ~=
"table"` is true and the whole record is rejected as malformed — even though
every other field decoded fine.

## Fix

Treat a missing `labels` key as an empty list instead of a decode failure,
e.g.:

```lua
or (issue.labels ~= nil and type(issue.labels) ~= "table")
```

and default `labels = issue.labels or {}` when building the returned table
(~line 72-86, the `for index, label in ipairs(issue.labels)` loop already
handles an empty/absent table fine once the type check stops rejecting it).

Filed during manual QA round, case 1 revisit (session
claude/827084e2-cc79-4a54-a8f4-3229ce4bcbc5 or nearby — reported inline, not
tied to a specific case number). Not fixed yet.
close_reason: fixed in 8aa5afd

title: Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it; louiselm attribution unproven
description:
The Ghostty terminal emulator died at 2026-08-20 05:14:18, taking all three of
its surfaces — and every Neovim inside them — with it. Neovim did not crash.
Attribution to louiselm is UNPROVEN and currently looks unlikely; this bead
exists so the next occurrence is diagnosable and so the round's record is
honest about what happened.

CORRECTION: this bead was originally filed as "Neovim dies with no crash
artifact". That was wrong, and the correction is the finding. Neovim was the
victim, not the subject.

## Observed

Session `cae87c06-bd44-429f-823e-6b18a361129f`, cwd `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`,
Neovim 0.12.2, Ghostty 1.3.1 (ReleaseFast, GTK 4.18.6, OpenGL renderer, AMDGPU
under gdm-x-session), build under test `cd37ab2`.

User's report: "i saw all nvim windows closing without me doing anything, that's
all, i didnt see a banner it was fast."

From `journalctl --user`:

```
05:02:28  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 481451)
05:02:29  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-481516.scope
05:04:29  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-483272.scope
05:10:20  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 488289)
05:10:20  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-488332.scope
05:14:18  app-ghostty-surface-transient-481516.scope: Consumed 1.110s CPU, 48.8M peak
05:14:18  app-ghostty-surface-transient-483272.scope: Consumed 7.435s CPU, 299.4M peak
05:14:19  app-ghostty-surface-transient-488332.scope: Consumed 7.578s CPU, 305.3M peak
05:14:27  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 491455)  <- fresh process
```

Three surface scopes terminating inside one second is the whole application
dying, not three windows being closed. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface —
confirmed at 05:16:59, where a new `ghostty` invocation (pid 493960) handed the
new surface to the already-running pid 491455 rather than starting its own.

Process start times agree: ghostty 491455 at 05:14:27, Neovim 491984 at
05:14:38 — the terminal came back eleven seconds before the editor was
relaunched inside it.

The agent side saw only the downstream effect
(`20260820-045809-478664-claude-agent-acp-stderr.log`):

```
Session cae87c06-...: query stream error: ACP connection closed
Error during cleanup: Error: Query closed before response received
```

with the JSON-RPC log ending on a pending `Edit` tool call
(`toolu_01K7RgEDmrCMf8NSaAEHEYLb`).

## Symptoms

- Every Neovim window vanishes simultaneously, instantly, with no message.
- No "Vim: Caught deadly signal" banner, because there was no deadly signal:
  Neovim's pty was hung up when its terminal died.
- Orphaned language servers accumulate (14 `copilot-language-server` at
  `ppid=1`, ~228 MB each) from instances killed this way.

## Root cause

Unknown for Ghostty. Established for Neovim: it was hung up, not crashed.

Ruled out by evidence:

- **Neovim crash.** No `ERR` in `~/.local/state/nvim/nvim.log` around
  05:08-05:14, only `tui_handle_term_mode` warnings. The surface scopes died
  first.
- **OOM kill.** `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/memory.events` reads
  `oom_kill 0`; `memory.max` is `max`; peak 13.1 GB of 27 GB. No cgroup in
  `user.slice` has a nonzero `oom_kill`.
- **Ghostty panic.** A Zig panic writes a trace to stderr, which reaches the
  journal — the journal has ghostty's full lifecycle for that window and no
  panic. Silent death points at a signal with no handler output.
- **`cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start`.** The user's config
  (`~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/treesitter.lua:138-151`) already ran
  `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so a markdown highlighter was
  attached to the chat buffer before the commit too. Net treesitter load is
  unchanged. Do not spend a round here.

Remaining hypotheses:

1. **Ghostty defect, unrelated to louiselm.** Base rate for this is high and
   nothing yet contradicts it. Discriminator: whether it recurs with no
   louiselm session attached.
2. **image.nvim's kitty graphics traffic crashing Ghostty.**
   `~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/image.lua` sets `backend = "kitty"`, so
   image.nvim writes kitty graphics escape sequences directly into Ghostty. The
   thread is thin: `cd37ab2` is supposed to have detached image.nvim from the
   transcript buffer, and the deaths happened on that build. It stays alive only
   if the detach is incomplete. Discriminator: QA case 1.2 of this round — list
   the chat buffer's autocmds and check for an image.nvim group. That case has
   not been run yet (it hit a recipe bug in the plan).
3. **GPU/driver fault.** AMDGPU with GLAMOR under X. `~/.local/share/xorg/Xorg.0.log`
   has nothing past boot, but a GPU reset lands in the kernel log, which is not
   readable here — the user is not in `adm`/`systemd-journal`, so
   `journalctl -k` returns nothing. Discriminator: `sudo dmesg | grep -i
   "amdgpu\|ring.*timeout\|GPU reset"` around 05:14.

## Why it was not caught

Not a test-suite gap — no suite can observe its own terminal emulator dying.
The real gap is that three of the four recording paths were off:

- `ulimit -c` is `0`, so neither Ghostty nor Neovim can write a core.
- `systemd-coredump` is not installed; `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` is the
  bare string `core`, so a dump would land in the process's cwd unnoticed.
- Neovim's deadly-signal message goes to stderr, i.e. the terminal that just
  died, and is never written to `NVIM_LOG_FILE`.

The path that *did* work — `journalctl --user`, which recorded Ghostty's whole
lifecycle — is the only reason this was diagnosable at all, and it was not
consulted first because the symptom was reported as a Neovim crash.

## Fix direction

Nothing in `lua/louiselm/` to change yet. In order:

1. `sudo dmesg` filtered for `amdgpu`/GPU reset around 05:14:18, to settle
   hypothesis 3 with the one log that was unreadable.
2. Run QA case 1.2 to settle hypothesis 2.
3. Install `systemd-coredump` (Debian) so the next Ghostty death leaves a
   stack, and set `ulimit -c unlimited` for interactive shells.
4. If it recurs and 1-2 come back clean, this is a Ghostty bug and belongs
   upstream, not here. Close it with the evidence rather than leaving it open
   in louiselm's graph.

Rejected: reverting or altering `cd37ab2` on suspicion. The evidence points
away from it, and it is the only build for which a full timeline exists.

## Acceptance

- Either a mechanism in `lua/louiselm/` with `file:line`, or a decision to
  close this as not-louiselm with the evidence that shows it.
- A recurrence after step 3 produces a durable artifact (coredump entry or
  captured stderr) rather than a silent disappearance.

## Not covered

- Whether the Neovim restarts at 05:08:39 and 05:11:02 were also Ghostty
  deaths is not established. The journal shows a ghostty start at 05:10:20 but
  the window before that is not reconstructed.
- The kernel log for 05:14 has not been read.
- The 14 orphaned copilot processes date from the previous evening's instances;
  they evidence unclean exits generally, not this specific death.
close_reason: Closed as not-LouiseLM: kernel log proves Ghostty renderer general-protection fault at the exact incident timestamp.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Instrumentation in place; hypothesis 3 (GPU/driver fault) ruled out. systemd-coredump installed; ulimit -c unlimited + nvim stderr-tee added to ~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc, both verified (deliberate SIGSEGV wrote core.507791; wrapper captured a simulated stderr line and still passed it through). dmesg amdgpu grep returns only boot-time lines (t=0.000000-3.557204); boot messages still present so the ring buffer has not wrapped, making the absence a real negative. Next cheapest discriminator: that grep would not match a userspace segfault, which the kernel logs as 'segfault at'/'traps:'. Run: sudo dmesg | grep -iE 'segfault|traps|general protection|protection fault' -- a ghostty[488289] line near 05:14:18 would settle attribution outright.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Hypothesis 2 (image.nvim kitty-graphics traffic crashing Ghostty) is ruled out. QA case 1.2 ran on build cd37ab2: the chat buffer's autocmd list contains no image.nvim group, so image.nvim is genuinely detached from the transcript buffer and is not writing kitty graphics escape sequences on its behalf. Case 1.3 independently confirms the per-keystroke lag is gone. Caveat on strength: the tester read the list and reported no image group rather than pasting it, so this rests on their reading, not on the raw output.

With hypotheses 2 and 3 both dead and no Neovim-side mechanism left, nothing now connects this crash to louiselm. Remaining discriminator is entirely outside this repo: 'sudo dmesg | grep -iE "segfault|traps|general protection|protection fault"' for a ghostty[488289] line near 05:14:18. If that is empty too, Ghostty exited without a signal the kernel noticed, and this should be closed as not-louiselm and taken upstream.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Final discriminator attempted 2026-08-20: sudo -n dmesg was denied because a password is required. coredumpctl has no Ghostty entry (capture was installed after the incident). User journal for 05:13:30-05:15:00 still shows only all three surface scopes ending and Ghostty restarting, with no panic/fault line. Owner must run: sudo dmesg --time-format iso | grep -iE "ghostty|segfault|traps|general protection|protection fault". If empty, close as not-LouiseLM; if it contains ghostty[488289] near 05:14:18, take the fault upstream.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Owner supplied the final kernel discriminator: `2026-08-20T05:14:18,312439+02:00 traps: renderer[249898] general protection fault ... in ghostty[...]`. The timestamp exactly matches all Ghostty surfaces terminating. `renderer[249898]` is the crashing thread name/TID; the mapped executable is Ghostty. This conclusively attributes the incident to a native fault in Ghostty, not Neovim or LouiseLM. Take any recurrence/coredump upstream to Ghostty.

title: agent process-handle return types annotated userdata? instead of vim.SystemObj?
description:
lua/louiselm/agent/spawn.lua (M.start), lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua (M.check),
and lua/louiselm/agent/init.lua (M.start, M.check) all annotate the
vim.system() process handle they return as `---@return userdata? handle`.
The real Neovim runtime stub (vim/_core/system.lua) declares vim.system's
async-form return type as `vim.SystemObj` (a plain Lua table with a
metatable), not `userdata`.

Evidence: adding a second `pcall(vim.system, ...)` call site in
lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua (for louiselm-2ce, the latest-version
staleness check) made `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`
newly report:

  lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:150:12 [Warning] Annotations specify that
    return value #1 has a type of `userdata?`, returning value of type
    `table` here instead. (return-type-mismatch)
  lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:193:10 [Warning] ... same ...
  lua/louiselm/agent/spawn.lua:49:10 [Warning] ... same ...

Bisected: the mismatch is pre-existing in spawn.lua's M.start and
health.lua's original (single-call) M.check — confirmed by reverting only
the new health.lua code and rerunning the check, which still flags
health.lua:102 (the untouched original --version call) and spawn.lua:49.
lua-language-server apparently didn't surface it before some threshold of
project analysis was crossed; it is a real annotation defect regardless of
when it is reported.

Fix: change `userdata?` to `vim.SystemObj?` in all four declarations so the
LuaCATS annotation matches vim.system()'s real return type.
close_reason: Fixed: changed userdata? to table? in lua/louiselm/agent/{spawn,health,init}.lua (matches pcall(vim.system,...)'s real inferred return type in this workspace's lua-language-server config, which doesn't expose vim.SystemObj). Also fixed a related latent duplicate-set-field warning uncovered by the same deeper analysis pass: converted direct 'nvim.system = ...'/'nvim.fn.executable = ...' stub reassignment to rawset() in tests/capture_spec.lua, tests/session/api_spec.lua, and tests/ui/command_spec.lua, matching the codebase's existing rawset(nvim, "notify", ...) convention. lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning now reports the same 9 pre-existing problems as a clean main checkout (all in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua, unrelated), confirmed stable across repeated runs.

title: Publish trademark policy with named-class refusal
description:
Publish a trademark policy for the LouiseLM name.

Under MIT this is the **only instrument that bites from day one**. MIT grants everyone the right to use the code; it conveys no right to the name. The policy is where the political line is actually drawn and enforced.

## Content

- The LouiseLM name and any associated marks are not licensed by the MIT grant and are reserved.
- Forks may say they are derived from LouiseLM. They may not present themselves as LouiseLM.
- Named class refusal: no permission to use the mark will be granted to *entities deriving a majority of revenue from proprietary foundation models, or from the hardware they run on.*
- Individuals, non-profits, educational institutions, worker-owned co-ops, and community projects are welcome to use the name to refer to the project.

## Why a class and not a list of companies

A list of company names is precise today and stale in eighteen months, and it is defeated by a rename or a subsidiary. A structural definition catches successors, cannot be gamed as easily, and states a principle rather than a grudge — which is also the difference between an anti-capitalist position and a feud with two firms.

## Acceptance criteria

- Policy document exists and is linked from README.
- The class is defined structurally, with no company named.
- The document is plain prose, readable in under two minutes. Precedents worth skimming for tone: Mozilla, Rust, Debian.
close_reason: Completed concise trademark policy and README link; documentary verification passed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Implemented TRADEMARK_POLICY.md and linked it from README.md. The 317-word policy reserves the LouiseLM marks, permits truthful reference and derived-from attribution, requires forks to use their own identity, states the structural majority-revenue class refusal without naming companies, and explicitly preserves identical software-licence rights for the refused class. Verification: git diff --check passed; Markdown targets exist; no named company appears in the policy.

title: Comment in-progress-first triage requirement onto workflow-engine issues
description:
Attach the in-progress-first triage requirement to the deferred workflow-engine issues as `br` comments, so it is discoverable from the issues themselves rather than from a conversation transcript.

## The requirement

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot express.

## The evidence behind it

`bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum across eight components. Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for `in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight, and a fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic comfortably. Observed in this repo: roughly 0.459 against 0.405.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix it. `priority-first` raises Urgency only to about 0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file. So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration — it has to be applied on top of its output, which is exactly why it belongs in the engine that consumes that output.

## Where it goes

Comment on the deferred workflow-engine issues — the ones covering persisted declarative workflows and sequential execution of beads graphs by policy-controlled agents. Both sit under the attention-control-plane epic.

Frame it as a **candidate requirement for that design conversation, not a decision already made.** The sequencing policy is the engine's to define; this records why the question exists and what the evidence was.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both relevant deferred issues carry a comment stating the requirement and the scoring evidence.
- The comment is explicit that this is input to a future design decision rather than a settled one.
- `br sync --flush-only` has been run so the comments reach JSONL and are committed.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: QA round: replayed user prompts on resume
description:
# Manual QA review — replayed user prompts on resume

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `110e357` (fix), on top of the permission-decision round
verified at `7d115d7`. `0dcdce5` (beads bookkeeping only) needs no testing.

Origin: `louiselm-pmr` — after `:LouiselmResume`, the chat showed the agent's
replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but silently dropped every
prompt the user had typed, so a resumed session read as one-sided. Root cause:
`lifecycle.lua` already turned the ACP `user_message_chunk` replay notification
into a `user_chunk` event (since `4e4a58b`), but `chat/init.lua`'s
`handle_event` never had a branch for it and dropped it on the floor. `110e357`
adds that branch, rendering each line prefixed `> `.

The unit test in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` proves the rendering logic against a
synthetic `fake_session` emitting a synthetic `user_chunk` event. It cannot
prove that a real adapter's replay actually looks like that, and it cannot
prove a *live* turn doesn't now render the user's prompt twice — both of
those only exist once a real `claude-agent-acp` process is in the loop.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls | **passed** — log + visual, see below |
| 2 | Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once | **passed** — log + visual, see below |

## Setup

The plugin is installed as a clone of this repo, so new commits are not live
until you update it:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

Confirm the clone matches the source, then restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

Both must print `110e357 fix(chat): show replayed user prompts`.

## Ground rules learned the hard way (carried over from prior rounds)

- Say the tool name and give absolute paths in prompts, or the model reaches
  for the wrong tool / does a `find` first and you burn a round trip.
- Start each case in a fresh session — a prior denial or detour in the same
  session makes the model hedge on the next one.
- Pin the adapter log by session id, not by mtime — the newest log file is
  whatever session you're talking to me in right now:
  ```bash
  L=$(grep -l "<session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
  ```
  The session id is in the chat header, or via `:LouiselmSessionId`.
- **That grep pollutes itself.** If *I* run it to pull evidence, my own bash
  command containing the session id gets logged into whatever log file is
  currently open for *this* conversation — `tail -1` then picks my own
  self-reference instead of the real target log. Fix: search all matching
  files, not just the last one, and eyeball which one actually has protocol
  content (`session/update` with real `sessionUpdate` kinds) rather than a
  `rawInput`/`toolCallId` echo of the grep command itself. Hit this pulling
  evidence for case 1.

## Cases

### 1. Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls

Exercises `110e357` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1305` against a real
`claude-agent-acp` replay, which is the exact shape the original bug report
had: two user turns with agent activity (including a tool call) between them.

Steps:

1. Start a **fresh** session in this repo.
2. Send: `Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md, then reply with just the word "ack".`
3. Once it replies, send a second prompt: `Now reply with just the word "ack2".`
4. Note the session id (`:LouiselmSessionId`), then `:LouiselmCloseSession`.
5. `:LouiselmResume` and pick that session.

Expect: the buffer shows, in original order: `> Use the Read tool...`, the
tool call line for the Read, the assistant's `ack`, `> Now reply...`, the
assistant's `ack2` — both prompts visible, prefixed `> `, in the order they
were actually sent, not collapsed or reordered relative to the tool call.

Failure signature: either prompt missing from the replay, both prompts shown
adjacent to each other instead of interleaved with the reply/tool call, or
prompt text without the `> ` prefix (i.e. the old "renders replayed assistant
chunks" behavior, meaning the fix didn't ship).

**Result: passed.** Session `claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`,
user reported the buffer looked right. Log evidence from
`20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` (the resume,
2 minutes after the original turn) confirms the wire order matches exactly
what case 1 predicted:

```
user_message_chunk "[@AGENTS.md](...)"
user_message_chunk "Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read ... ack"
tool_call Read AGENTS.md (pending)
tool_call_update (completed)
agent_message_chunk "ack"
user_message_chunk "Now reply with just the word \"ack2\"."
agent_message_chunk "ack2"
```

Both prompts present, correctly interleaved around the Read tool call, in
original order. Combined with the user's visual read of the buffer, this
closes the "does a real adapter's replay actually look like the synthetic
unit-test fixture" question the unit test structurally can't answer.

### 2. Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once

Exercises the regression the bead flagged as unverified: `handle_event` now
has a branch for `user_chunk`, so this checks a *live* `claude-agent-acp` turn
never also emits `user_message_chunk` (which `submit_prompt` already writes
into the buffer directly — a second write would duplicate it).

Steps:

1. In any session (resumed or fresh), submit: `Reply with just the word "once".`

Expect: the prompt line `> Reply with just the word "once".` appears exactly
once in the buffer, followed by exactly one `once` response.

Failure signature: the prompt text appears twice (once from `submit_prompt`,
once from a `user_chunk` event the live turn shouldn't have produced).

**Result: passed.** User ran this in the same resumed session
(`claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`, reusing the adapter process
from case 1) and confirmed the buffer looked right. Log evidence from the
same `20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`, appended
after the case-1 replay (lines 9-17, the live "once" turn): `agent_message_chunk
'once'` and nothing else — no `user_message_chunk` for the "once" prompt.
Grand total `user_message_chunk` count for the whole file stayed at 3 (the two

grep -c '"user_message_chunk"' "$L"
